20372.q: What is the federal office in Switzerland where you can report phishing and cyberattacks called?
20372.e: The Federal Office for Cyber Security (NCSC) has existed since 2024. It receives reports of cyber incidents and warns about new scams.
20372.m: I can report phishing to the Federal Office for Cyber Security.

20373.q: What should you do before clicking on a link in a suspicious email?
a: Hover the mouse over it and check the real address
20373.e: When you hover over it, the program shows the real target address. If it does not match the company, the link is fake.
20373.m: I check a link's address before I click.

a: Targeted phishing aimed at a particular person
Phishing with adverts for fishing gear
20374.e: In spear phishing, fraudsters tailor the message exactly to one person, for example with their name and real details. That makes it hard to recognise.
20374.m: Targeted scam messages can look very real.

a: A fake online shop that delivers nothing after payment
20375.e: Fake shops lure people with very low prices and demand payment in advance. The goods never arrive.
20375.m: If an offer is too good to be true, it is often a scam.

20376.q: What is a sign of a fake shop?
a: No legal notice and payment in advance only
20376.e: Genuine shops have a legal notice with an address and offer safe ways to pay. If both are missing, be careful.
20376.m: An online shop without a legal notice is suspicious.

a: A scam where feelings are faked to get money
A love film on the internet
A dating app for older people
20377.e: Fraudsters build up a romantic relationship online and then ask for money, for example for a supposed emergency.
20377.m: If someone only knows me online and wants money, that is suspicious.

20378.q: What is typical of an advance-fee scam?
a: You are asked to pay money first to get more later
You get a bill straight away
You have to sign a contract
20378.e: Fraudsters promise a prize or an inheritance but ask for fees first. The promised amount never comes.
20378.m: If you have to pay first to get a prize, you are being cheated.

20379.q: What should you do if a so-called support worker calls and wants remote access to your computer?
a: Hang up and not allow access
20379.e: In support scams, criminals pretend to work for well-known companies. With remote access they steal data or money.
20379.m: I do not give strangers access to my computer.

20380.q: Someone on the internet threatens to publish something embarrassing about you if you do not pay. What do you do?
a: Not pay, keep evidence and get help
20380.e: People who pay are often blackmailed again. It is better to take screenshots, stop contact and get help from adults, from the number 147 or from the police.
20380.m: If I am blackmailed, I do not pay and get help straight away.

a: A login with a password and a second proof
20381.e: As well as the password, you need a second factor, such as a code from an app or by text message. This protects accounts even if the password is stolen.
20381.m: A second factor gives my account extra protection.

20382.q: What is a message saying “You have won a new phone, click here” most likely to be?
a: A system message from the phone
20382.e: Promises of prizes without entering a competition are a classic trick. They lead to sites that grab data or money.

20383.q: How long is a work such as a book or a song protected by copyright in Switzerland?
a: Until 70 years after the creator's death
Until 25 years after the creator's death
20383.e: The Copyright Act protects works until 70 years after the death of the creator. After that they are in the public domain.
20383.m: Works are protected until 70 years after the creator's death.

20384.q: Can you simply copy a computer game you bought and sell the copies on the internet?
a: Yes, if it is more than a year old
Yes, if you lower the price
20384.e: Computer programs and games are protected by copyright. Anyone who copies and passes them on or sells them breaks the makers' rights.
20384.m: I may not copy and sell games I have bought.

20385.q: Who holds the copyright to a photo you took yourself?
a: The platform where it is shown
20385.e: Copyright belongs automatically to the person who creates a work. No registration is needed.
20385.m: Whoever creates a work holds the copyright to it.

20386.q: In Switzerland, what is the case when uploading copyrighted music without permission?
a: It is only allowed on Sundays
It is allowed if you share it
20386.e: Downloading music and films for your own use is allowed, but offering and uploading them without permission is not.
20386.m: I may not simply offer other people's music online.

a: Permissions with which creators allow use under conditions
20387.e: With Creative Commons, creators can decide how others may use their work, for example only with credit or not for commercial purposes.
20387.m: Creative Commons licences allow use under certain conditions.

20388.q: What does “BY” mean in a Creative Commons licence?
a: The creator's name must be given
The work is only for authorities
20388.e: BY requires attribution. Anyone who uses the work must say who it comes from.
20388.m: With CC BY, I always name the creator.

20389.q: What must you remember when quoting from someone else's text?
20389.e: Quotations are allowed if they serve to explain something and are marked as quotations. The source must be named.
20389.m: When I quote, I always give the source.

a: A work is no longer protected by copyright
A work belongs to the municipality
A work may only be read
20390.e: Once the protection period is over, anyone may use a work freely, for example Mozart's music.
20390.m: Anyone may use works in the public domain freely.

20391.q: What does the right to your own image mean?
a: You can basically decide yourself whether photos of you are published
You may use all photos on the internet
You must pay for every photo
20391.e: The right to your own image is part of the protection of personal rights. Anyone who wants to publish a photo of a recognisable person usually needs their consent.
20391.m: Before I post a photo of someone, I ask for permission.

20392.q: In which Swiss law is the protection of personal rights, which includes the right to your own image, laid down?
20392.e: Article 28 of the Civil Code protects personal rights against unlawful violation. The right to your own image is derived from it.
20392.m: The Civil Code protects my personal rights.

20393.q: What should you do before putting a class group photo online?
a: Make the photo black and white
Nothing, group photos are always allowed
20393.e: Every recognisable person has the right to their own image. That is why you need everyone's consent, and for children their parents' too.
20393.m: For a group photo, I ask everyone who is in it.

20394.q: What can you demand if a photo of you was published without permission?
20394.e: If the right to your own image is violated, you can demand its removal and contact the platform or, if necessary, a court.
20394.m: I can have photos of me that were posted without permission deleted.

20395.q: For children under 14, who usually also has to agree before a photo is published?
20395.e: Younger children often cannot yet judge the consequences of a photo being published. That is why their parents help decide.
20395.m: For younger children, parents help decide about photos.

20396.q: When is the consent of the person in a photo usually not needed to publish it?
a: When they only appear in the background of a large crowd
When the photo is black and white
When they are looking at the camera
When the photo was taken in your own garden
20396.e: If a person is only in a picture by chance and in the background, for example in a crowd at a festival, their personal rights are usually not violated. If they are the focus, their consent is usually needed.
20396.m: Anyone who is the focus of a photo usually has to be asked.

20397.q: Can you secretly film people at a swimming pool and share the video?
a: No, that violates their personal rights
Yes, if the video is short
Yes, if you only send it to friends
20397.e: Secret recordings of people in private or intimate situations violate their personal rights and can be a criminal offence.

20398.q: What is meant by digital identity?
a: All the features by which you are recognised online
The serial number of your phone
20398.e: Digital identity includes usernames, profiles, passwords, photos and data linked to a person on the internet.
20398.m: My digital identity is made up of everything that makes me who I am online.

a: A long password with different characters
20399.e: Long passwords with letters, numbers and special characters are hard to guess. Personal details are easy to find out.
20399.m: A good password is long and hard to guess.

20400.q: Why should you not use the same password for all your accounts?
a: Because then a data leak puts all accounts at risk
Because it is against the law
20400.e: If a password is stolen, attackers often try it on lots of services. Different passwords limit the damage.
20400.m: I use a separate password for every account.

20401.q: What is a password manager for?
a: It stores lots of passwords securely encrypted
20401.e: A password manager remembers lots of strong passwords. You only need to remember one master password.
20401.m: A password manager helps me use many secure passwords.

20402.q: What is identity theft on the internet?
a: Someone uses another person's data to pretend to be them
20402.e: Criminals open accounts or order goods in the victim's name, for example. To do this they use stolen personal data.
20402.m: I protect my data so that nobody can pretend to be me.

20403.q: What did Swiss voters decide in September 2025 about the state e-ID?
a: They did not vote at all
20403.e: On 28 September 2025, the federal law on electronic identity was narrowly accepted with about 50.4 per cent voting yes. The e-ID is issued by the federal government, is voluntary and, according to the Federal Council, is due to start at the end of 2026.
20403.m: Switzerland is introducing a voluntary state e-ID.

a: An account with a false identity
A profile with lots of photos
20404.e: Fake profiles pretend to be someone else, often with stolen photos. They are used for scams, bullying or advertising.
20404.m: Not every profile belongs to the person it shows.

a: A graphic figure that represents a person online
A virus in an email attachment
20405.e: An avatar is a profile picture or game character. It can help you avoid showing your own face online.
20405.m: With an avatar I do not have to show my real face.

a: Being able to use media sensibly, critically and responsibly
Owning as many devices as possible
Being able to type as fast as possible
Having as many followers as possible
20406.e: Media literacy includes understanding, judging and creating media. It helps you find your way safely in the world of media.
20406.m: Media literacy means using media wisely.

20407.q: What is part of media literacy?
a: Checking information from the media critically
Being on your phone as long as possible
20407.e: People who are media literate can use, understand, judge and create media. The German educator Dieter Baacke shaped the idea.
20407.m: Media literate people use media wisely and critically.

20408.q: What is the module in the Swiss “Lehrplan 21” curriculum in which pupils learn media literacy called?
20408.e: The “Media and Computer Science” module of Lehrplan 21 covers media education, computer science and user skills.
20408.m: In Lehrplan 21, media literacy is learnt in the Media and Computer Science module.

20409.q: According to Swiss studies, which device do almost all young people aged 12 to 19 use every day?
20409.e: The JAMES study by the ZHAW surveys young people in Switzerland every two years. Almost all of them have their own phone and use it every day.
20409.m: The mobile phone is the most important media device for Swiss young people.

20410.q: What can you find in the legal notice (imprint) of a website?
a: Details of who is responsible for the site
20410.e: The legal notice gives the name and address of the operators. It helps you judge how trustworthy a site is.
20410.m: The legal notice says who is behind a website.

20411.q: How can you tell that a website is more likely to be trustworthy?
a: It names sources and has a legal notice
It has lots of colourful pictures
It asks for your password straight away
20411.e: Genuine sites show who is behind them and back up their statements with sources. The federal government's “Youth and Media” platform, for example, offers tips on this.
20411.m: Trustworthy sites name sources and the people responsible.

20412.q: What is a good strategy against too much screen time?
a: Charging your phone next to your pillow at night
20412.e: Phone-free times, for example at meals or before sleeping, help you control your media use consciously.
20412.m: Phone-free times help me use media consciously.

20413.q: What is the difference between a news article and a comment piece in a newspaper?
a: The comment piece gives a personal opinion
The comment piece is always longer
The comment piece has no headline
The comment piece only contains numbers
20413.e: A news article reports on events as factually as possible. A comment piece is marked as an opinion article.
20413.m: News reports, comment pieces give opinions.

20812.q: What is the German word ‘Hallo’ in English?
20812.e: In English you say ‘Hello’ when you greet someone.

20813.q: What is the German greeting ‘Guten Morgen’ in English?
20813.e: ‘Morgen’ means morning, so in the morning you say ‘Good morning’.
20813.m: In the morning you say ‘Guten Morgen’, or ‘Good morning’.

20814.q: What is the German ‘Gute Nacht’ in English?
20814.e: Before going to sleep, you say ‘Good night’ in English and ‘Gute Nacht’ in German.
20814.m: Before sleeping you wish someone ‘Good night’.

20815.q: What is the German ‘Auf Wiedersehen’ in English?
20815.e: When you leave, you say ‘Goodbye’ or just ‘Bye’ in English.

20816.q: What is the German word ‘Danke’ in English?
20816.e: When you thank someone, you say ‘Thank you’ or just ‘Thanks’ in English.

20817.q: What is the German word ‘Bitte’ in English when you ask for something?
20817.e: When you politely ask for something, you say ‘please’ in English.
20817.m: Polite children say ‘bitte’ in German and ‘please’ in English.

20819.q: What is the German sentence ‘Ich heisse Anna’ in English?
20819.e: When you introduce yourself in English, you say ‘My name is ...’.
20819.m: With ‘My name is’ you tell someone your name in English.

20820.q: What is the German number ‘eins’ in English?
20820.e: The number 1 is ‘eins’ in German and ‘one’ in English.

20821.q: What is the German number ‘drei’ in English?
20821.e: The number 3 is ‘drei’ in German and ‘three’ in English. A ‘tree’ is something quite different.

20822.q: What is the German number ‘fünf’ in English?
20822.e: The number 5 is ‘fünf’ in German and ‘five’ in English.

20823.e: ‘Seven’ is the English word for the number 7. It sounds similar to the German ‘sieben’.

20824.q: What is the German number ‘zehn’ in English?
20824.e: The number 10 is ‘zehn’ in German and ‘ten’ in English.

20825.e: ‘Eight’ is the English word for the number 8. In German it is ‘acht’.

20826.q: What is the German number ‘zwölf’ in English?
20826.e: The number 12 is ‘twelve’ in English. It sounds a little like the German ‘zwölf’.

20827.e: ‘Twenty’ is the English word for the number 20. In German it is ‘zwanzig’.

20828.q: What is ‘two plus two’ in English words?
20828.e: Two plus two makes four, and in English you write it as ‘four’.

20829.q: What is the German colour ‘rot’ in English?
20829.e: The colour ‘rot’ in German is ‘red’ in English.

20830.q: What is the German colour ‘blau’ in English?
20830.e: The colour ‘blau’ in German is ‘blue’ in English.

20831.q: What is the German colour ‘grün’ in English?
20831.e: The colour ‘grün’ in German is ‘green’ in English. Grass is green.

20832.q: What is the German colour ‘gelb’ in English?
20832.e: The colour ‘gelb’ in German is ‘yellow’ in English. People often paint the sun yellow.

20833.e: ‘Black’ is ‘schwarz’ in German. The night is often black.

20834.q: What is the German colour ‘weiss’ in English?
20834.e: The colour ‘weiss’ in German is ‘white’ in English. Snow is white.

20835.e: ‘Brown’ is ‘braun’ in German. Chocolate is usually brown.

20836.q: What is the German colour ‘violett’ in English?
20836.e: The colour ‘violett’ in German is usually ‘purple’ in English.

20837.e: ‘Grey’ is ‘grau’ in German. An elephant is grey.

20838.q: What is the German word ‘Hund’ in English?
20838.e: The German word ‘Hund’ means ‘dog’ in English.

20839.q: What is the German word ‘Katze’ in English?
20839.e: The German word ‘Katze’ means ‘cat’ in English.

20841.q: What is the German word ‘Kuh’ in English?
20841.e: The German word ‘Kuh’ means ‘cow’. In Switzerland you see lots of cows in the meadows.

20842.e: ‘Bird’ is ‘Vogel’ in German. Most birds can fly.

20843.q: What is the German word ‘Maus’ in English?
20843.e: The German word ‘Maus’ means ‘mouse’ in English.

20844.e: ‘Fish’ is ‘Fisch’ in German. Fish live in water.

20845.q: What is the German word ‘Schwein’ in English?
20845.e: The German word ‘Schwein’ means ‘pig’ in English.

20846.e: ‘Rabbit’ is ‘Kaninchen’ in German. A hare, on the other hand, is ‘Hase’.

20847.q: What is the German word ‘Mutter’ in English?
20847.e: The German word ‘Mutter’ means ‘mother’; people often say ‘mum’.

20848.q: What is the German word ‘Vater’ in English?
20848.e: The German word ‘Vater’ means ‘father’; people often say ‘dad’.

20849.q: How do you say ‘my sister’ in German?
20849.e: ‘Sister’ is ‘Schwester’ in German. She is a girl with the same parents.

20850.q: What is the German word ‘Bruder’ in English?
20850.e: The German word ‘Bruder’ means ‘brother’ in English.

20851.q: What is the German word ‘Grossmutter’ in English?
20851.e: The German word ‘Grossmutter’ means ‘grandmother’, or ‘granny’ for short.

20852.q: How do you say ‘my grandfather’ in German?
20852.e: A grandfather is the father of your mum or dad. In German he is the ‘Grossvater’.

20853.q: What is the German word ‘Tante’ in English?
20853.e: The German word ‘Tante’ means ‘aunt’. An ‘ant’ is an insect.

20854.q: What is the German word ‘Familie’ in English?
20854.e: The German word ‘Familie’ means ‘family’ in English.

20855.q: What is the German word ‘Kopf’ in English?
20855.e: The German word ‘Kopf’ means ‘head’ in English.

20856.q: What is the German word ‘Bein’ in English?
20856.e: The German word ‘Bein’ means ‘leg’. We walk and run with our legs.

20857.e: ‘Nose’ is ‘Nase’ in German. We smell with it.

20858.q: What is the German word ‘Auge’ in English?
20858.e: The German word ‘Auge’ means ‘eye’. We see with our eyes.

20859.e: ‘Mouth’ is ‘Mund’ in German. We eat and speak with our mouth.

20860.q: What is the German word ‘Fuss’ in English?
20860.e: The German word ‘Fuss’ means ‘foot’. More than one foot are ‘feet’.

20861.e: ‘Ear’ is ‘Ohr’ in German. We hear with our ears.

20862.q: What is the German word ‘Haare’ in English?
20862.e: The German word ‘Haare’ means ‘hair’ in English.

20863.q: What is the German word ‘Apfel’ in English?
20863.e: The German word ‘Apfel’ means ‘apple’ in English.

20864.q: What is the German word ‘Brot’ in English?
20864.e: The German word ‘Brot’ means ‘bread’ in English.

20865.e: ‘Milk’ is ‘Milch’ in German. Swiss cows give a lot of milk.

20866.q: What is the German word ‘Käse’ in English?
20866.e: The German word ‘Käse’ means ‘cheese’. Switzerland is famous for its cheese.

20868.q: What is the German word ‘Ei’ in English?
20868.e: The German word ‘Ei’ means ‘egg’ in English.

20869.e: ‘Banana’ is ‘Banane’ in German. The word looks almost the same in both languages.

20870.q: What is the German word ‘Kuchen’ in English?
20870.e: The German word ‘Kuchen’ means ‘cake’. On birthdays there is often a birthday cake.

20871.q: What is the German word ‘Schuhe’ in English?
20871.e: The German word ‘Schuhe’ means ‘shoes’ in English.

20873.q: What is the German word ‘Socken’ in English?
20873.e: The German word ‘Socken’ means ‘socks’ in English.

20875.q: What is the German word ‘Kleid’ in English?
20875.e: The German word ‘Kleid’ means ‘dress’ in English.

20876.e: ‘Trousers’ is ‘Hose’ in German. In America people also say ‘pants’.

20877.q: What is the German word ‘Rock’ in English?
20877.e: The German word ‘Rock’ means ‘skirt’. A dress is ‘Kleid’ and a shirt is ‘Hemd’.

20878.e: ‘Gloves’ is ‘Handschuhe’ in German, literally ‘hand shoes’. In winter they keep your hands warm.

20879.q: What is the German word ‘Schule’ in English?
20879.e: The German word ‘Schule’ means ‘school’ in English.

20880.q: What is the German word ‘Buch’ in English?
20880.e: The German word ‘Buch’ means ‘book’ in English.

20882.q: What is the German word ‘Lehrerin’ in English?
20882.e: In German a female teacher is ‘Lehrerin’ and a male teacher ‘Lehrer’. In English both are ‘teacher’.

20883.q: Which German word means a ‘rubber’ at school?
20883.e: In Britain an eraser is called a ‘rubber’; in America it is an ‘eraser’. In German it is ‘Radiergummi’.

20884.q: What is the German word ‘Schultasche’ in English?
20884.e: The German word ‘Schultasche’ means ‘schoolbag’ in English.

20885.e: ‘Ruler’ is ‘Lineal’ in German. You use it to draw straight lines.

20886.q: What is the German word ‘Tisch’ in English?
20886.e: The German word ‘Tisch’ means ‘table’ in English.

20887.q: What is the German day ‘Montag’ in English?
20887.e: ‘Montag’ is ‘Monday’. In English the days of the week always start with a capital letter.

20888.e: ‘Friday’ is ‘Freitag’ in German. The two words sound similar.

20889.q: What is the German day ‘Sonntag’ in English?
20889.e: ‘Sonntag’ is ‘Sunday’. In both languages the word contains the sun: ‘Sonne’ and ‘sun’.

20891.q: What is the German day ‘Samstag’ in English?
20891.e: The German day ‘Samstag’ is ‘Saturday’ in English.

20892.e: ‘Tuesday’ is ‘Dienstag’ in German. It comes after Monday.

20893.q: What is the German day ‘Donnerstag’ in English?
20893.e: The German day ‘Donnerstag’ is ‘Thursday’ in English.

20894.q: What is the German word ‘Wochenende’ in English?
20894.e: Saturday and Sunday together make the weekend, in German ‘Wochenende’.

20895.q: What is the German month ‘Januar’ in English?
20895.e: ‘Januar’ is ‘January’. In English, months start with a capital letter.

20896.e: ‘May’ is ‘Mai’ in German. It is the fifth month of the year.

20897.q: What is the German month ‘Dezember’ in English?
20897.e: ‘Dezember’ is ‘December’. Many people celebrate Christmas in December.

20898.e: ‘March’ is ‘März’ in German. It is the third month of the year.

20899.q: What is the German month ‘Juni’ in English?
20899.e: ‘Juni’ is ‘June’. It is the sixth month of the year.

20900.e: ‘July’ is ‘Juli’ in German. It is the seventh month of the year.

20901.q: What is the German month ‘Oktober’ in English?
20901.e: ‘Oktober’ is ‘October’ in English, with a c instead of a k.

20902.q: What is the German word ‘Monat’ in English?
20902.e: The German word ‘Monat’ means ‘month’. The moon is ‘Mond’ in German.

20903.q: How do you say ‘Hello’ (good day) in French?
20903.e: To greet someone in French you say ‘Bonjour’. You hear it everywhere in French-speaking Switzerland.
20903.m: In French you greet someone with ‘Bonjour’.

20904.q: How do you say ‘Thank you’ in French?
20904.e: When you thank someone in French, you say ‘merci’. People in German-speaking Switzerland often say ‘merci’ too.
20904.m: In French you say thank you with ‘merci’.

20905.q: How do you say ‘yes’ in French?
20905.e: ‘Yes’ in French is ‘oui’. You pronounce it roughly like ‘wee’.
20905.m: The French word for yes is ‘oui’.

20906.q: How do you say ‘Goodbye’ in French?
20906.e: When you leave, you say ‘Au revoir’ in French.
20906.m: In French you say goodbye with ‘Au revoir’.

20907.e: The cat is ‘le chat’ in French.
20907.m: The cat is ‘le chat’ in French.

20908.q: How do you say ‘one, two, three’ in French?
20908.e: In French you count ‘un, deux, trois’. ‘Uno, dos, tres’ is Spanish and ‘uno, due, tre’ is Italian.
20908.m: In French you count ‘un, deux, trois’.

20909.e: ‘Rouge’ is the French word for red.
20909.m: The French ‘rouge’ is the colour red.

20910.e: Mother in French is ‘la mère’, with an accent on the first e (è). ‘La mer’ without an accent is the sea.
20910.m: The mother is ‘la mère’ in French.

20911.e: Bread is ‘le pain’ in French. At the bakery you might order ‘un pain’.

20912.q: What is the Swiss word ‘Velo’ in English?
20912.e: In Switzerland a bike is called a ‘Velo’. In English it is a ‘bicycle’ or ‘bike’; a ‘motorbike’ has an engine.
20912.m: A ‘Velo’ is a ‘bicycle’ or ‘bike’ in English.

20913.e: The kitchen is the room where you cook. In German it is ‘Küche’, and to cook is ‘kochen’.

20914.q: What is the German word ‘Schmetterling’ in English?
20914.e: A ‘Schmetterling’ is a butterfly. A dragonfly is ‘Libelle’ and a ladybird is ‘Marienkäfer’.

20915.e: The order is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, in German Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag. So ‘Wednesday’ is ‘Mittwoch’.

20916.q: Which English word is the opposite of ‘expensive’?
20916.e: ‘Cheap’ means costing little money and is the opposite of ‘expensive’.
20916.m: What is not expensive is cheap.

20917.q: What is the German word ‘Wolke’ in English?
20917.e: A ‘Wolke’ is a cloud. A crowd is a large group of people and a clock tells the time.

20918.e: After August comes September, just as in German.

20919.e: ‘Gross’ plus ‘Mutter’ makes ‘Grossmutter’, the grandmother. The grandfather is ‘Grossvater’.

20920.q: What is the Swiss word ‘Rüebli’ in English?
20920.e: In Switzerland a carrot is called a ‘Rüebli’. A cucumber and a cabbage are different vegetables.

20921.q: What does the French word ‘la gare’ mean?
20921.e: ‘La gare’ is the railway station, for example ‘la gare de Lausanne’.
20921.m: Trains leave from the station, the ‘gare’.

20922.q: What word do people in French-speaking Switzerland use for the number 90?
20922.e: In French-speaking Switzerland people say ‘nonante’ for 90. In France they say ‘quatre-vingt-dix’.
20922.m: In French-speaking Switzerland 70 is ‘septante’ and 90 is ‘nonante’.

20923.q: How do you say ‘Friday’ in French?
20923.e: The week goes lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. Friday is ‘vendredi’.

20924.q: What does the French word ‘la fenêtre’ mean?
20924.e: ‘La fenêtre’ is the window. The door is ‘la porte’.

20925.q: How do you say ‘red’ in French?
20925.e: Red is ‘rouge’. ‘Jaune’ is yellow, ‘vert’ green and ‘bleu’ blue.
20925.m: The colour red is ‘rouge’ in French.

20926.q: What does the French word ‘le frère’ mean?
20926.e: ‘Le frère’ is the brother and ‘la sœur’ the sister.
20926.m: My brother is ‘mon frère’ in French.

20928.q: What does ‘la pomme de terre’ mean?
20928.e: Literally it means ‘apple of the earth’, and it is the potato. The apple on its own is ‘la pomme’.
20928.m: A potato is ‘la pomme de terre’ in French.

20929.q: Which English sentence has the correct word order?
20929.e: English usually follows subject, verb, object. Time phrases like ‘every day’ go at the end or the start of the sentence.
20929.m: In an English sentence the subject is followed by the verb and then the object.

20930.e: In French, colour adjectives come after the noun, so ‘une voiture rouge’.
20930.m: In French the colour comes after the noun.

20931.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘She ___ a sister.’?
20931.e: With he, she and it, the present tense form of ‘to have’ is ‘has’.

20932.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Nous ___ à Berne.’?
20932.e: ‘Nous’ goes with the ending -ons, so ‘nous habitons’.
20932.m: Verbs with ‘nous’ usually end in -ons in the present tense.

a: There are three cats in the garden.
There is three cats in the garden.
It are three cats in the garden.
There be three cats in the garden.
20933.e: For several things you say ‘there are’, for one thing ‘there is’.
20933.m: For the plural you use ‘there are’.

20934.q: What does the sentence ‘Il fait beau aujourd'hui.’ mean?
20934.e: ‘Il fait beau’ describes nice weather, and ‘aujourd'hui’ means today.
20934.m: When the weather is nice, you say ‘il fait beau’ in French.

20935.q: Which indefinite article goes before ‘orange’ in English?
20935.e: Before words that start with a vowel sound you use ‘an’. ‘The’ is the definite article.

20936.q: Which article goes with the French word ‘maison’ (house)?
20936.e: ‘Maison’ is feminine and starts with a consonant, so it is ‘la maison’.
20936.m: The house is feminine in French: ‘la maison’.

20937.q: Which English question word asks about a place?
20937.e: ‘Where’ asks about a place. ‘When’ asks about time, ‘why’ about a reason and ‘who’ about a person.
20937.m: With ‘where’ you ask about a place.

20938.q: How do you ask ‘What's your name?’ in French?
20938.e: ‘S'appeler’ means to be called. With ‘Comment tu t'appelles ?’ you ask someone's name.
20938.m: You ask someone's name with ‘Comment tu t'appelles ?’.

20939.q: Which English question is formed correctly?
20939.e: In the present tense, questions are formed with ‘do’ or ‘does’. With ‘you’ it is ‘do’.
20939.m: English questions in the present tense are formed with ‘do’ or ‘does’.

20940.q: Which word is missing in the question ‘___ she play tennis?’?
20940.e: With he, she and it, a present tense question needs ‘does’. The main verb then stays in its base form.

20941.q: What does the French question word ‘pourquoi’ mean?
20941.e: ‘Pourquoi’ means why. The answer often starts with ‘parce que’ (because).
20941.m: The answer to ‘pourquoi’ often starts with ‘parce que’.

20942.q: How do you ask someone's age in French?
20942.e: In French you ‘have’ an age, so you ask ‘Quel âge as-tu ?’. The answer might be ‘J'ai douze ans’.
20942.m: In French you ask someone's age with ‘Quel âge as-tu ?’.

20943.q: Which word is missing in the question ‘___ much is this T-shirt?’?
20943.e: ‘How much’ asks about a price or an amount you cannot count.
20943.m: In English you ask about the price with ‘How much?’.

20944.q: Which words can start a yes/no question in French?
20944.e: ‘Est-ce que’ turns a statement into a yes/no question, for example ‘Est-ce que tu viens ?’.
20944.m: With ‘est-ce que’ a statement becomes a yes/no question.

20945.q: What is the negative of ‘I like fish.’?
20945.e: In the present tense you make negatives with ‘don't’ or ‘doesn't’. With ‘I’ it is ‘don't’.
20945.m: With ‘I’, ‘you’, ‘we’ and ‘they’ you use ‘don't’ for the negative.

20946.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘He ___ speak French.’?
20946.e: With he, she and it you make the present tense negative with ‘doesn't’. The verb stays in its base form.
20946.m: With ‘he’ you use ‘doesn't’ and the base form of the verb.

20947.q: What is the negative of ‘Je mange.’?
20947.e: In French, ‘ne’ and ‘pas’ go around the verb.
20947.m: In a French negative the verb sits between ‘ne’ and ‘pas’.

20948.q: What does ‘Je ne sais pas.’ mean?
20948.e: ‘Savoir’ means to know and ‘je sais’ means I know. With ‘ne ... pas’ it becomes ‘I don't know’.
20948.m: If you don't know something, you say ‘Je ne sais pas’ in French.

20949.q: What does the French negative ‘ne ... jamais’ mean?
20949.e: ‘Jamais’ means never. ‘Rien’ means nothing and ‘personne’ nobody.
20949.m: With ‘ne ... jamais’ you say ‘never’ in French.

20950.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘They ___ at home yesterday.’?
20950.e: ‘Yesterday’ needs the past tense of ‘to be’. With ‘they’ it is ‘were’, and the negative is ‘weren't’.
20950.m: With ‘they’ the negative past of ‘to be’ is ‘weren't’.

20951.q: What is the negative of ‘J'ai un chat.’?
a: Je ne pas ai un chat.
20951.e: Before a vowel ‘ne’ becomes ‘n'’. After the negative, ‘un’ usually becomes ‘de’.

20952.q: Which English sentence is a correct negative?
20952.e: With ‘I’ you use ‘don't’. A double negative like ‘haven't got no’ is wrong in standard English.
20952.m: In English you only use one negative per sentence.

20953.e: A sister is a female person, so you replace her with ‘she’.
20953.m: For a female person you use ‘she’ in English.

20954.q: Which English pronoun replaces ‘Tom and I’ as the subject?
20954.e: ‘Tom and I’ together are ‘we’ when they are the subject. ‘Us’ is the object form.
20954.m: I and another person together are ‘we’.

20955.q: Which French pronoun is often used instead of ‘nous’ in everyday speech?
20955.e: In everyday speech people often say ‘on’ for we, for example ‘On va au cinéma ?’. The verb is then in the third person singular.
20955.m: In everyday French many people say ‘on’ instead of ‘nous’.

20956.e: For a group made up only of females you use ‘elles’.
20956.m: In French you replace several girls or women with ‘elles’.

20957.q: What is the polite form of ‘you’ in French?
20957.e: ‘Vous’ is the polite form and also the plural of ‘tu’.
20957.m: In French you address adults you don't know well with ‘vous’.

20958.q: Which word is missing in the question ‘Can you help ___?’ when you mean yourself?
20958.e: After a verb you use the object form. The object form of ‘I’ is ‘me’.
20958.m: After a verb you use ‘me’ instead of ‘I’.

20959.q: Which French pronoun replaces ‘Marc et Julie’?
20959.e: As soon as a group includes a male person, you use ‘ils’.
20959.m: In French a mixed group is replaced with ‘ils’.

20960.q: What do you normally use the English pronoun ‘it’ for?
a: for a thing or an animal
20960.e: ‘It’ stands for things and usually also for animals. For people you use ‘he’ or ‘she’.
20960.m: In English you replace things with ‘it’.

20961.e: ‘To buy’ is ‘kaufen’ in German. ‘Verkaufen’ means to sell and ‘bezahlen’ to pay.

20962.q: What does the French verb ‘aller’ mean?
20962.e: ‘Aller’ means to go. It is irregular, for example ‘je vais’.
20962.m: The verb ‘aller’ means to go and is irregular.

20963.q: What does the French verb ‘faire’ mean?
20963.e: ‘Faire’ means to make or to do, for example ‘faire du sport’.
20963.m: If you do sport, you say ‘je fais du sport’ in French.

20964.e: ‘To forget’ is ‘vergessen’ in German. ‘Verlieren’ means to lose and ‘vermissen’ to miss.

20965.q: What does the French verb ‘prendre’ mean?
20965.e: ‘Prendre’ means to take, for example ‘prendre le train’. To give is ‘donner’.
20965.m: In French you take the train with ‘prendre le train’.

20966.e: ‘To understand’ is ‘verstehen’ in German. In English the past form is ‘understood’.

20967.q: What does the French verb ‘vouloir’ mean?
20967.e: ‘Vouloir’ means to want. The polite form ‘je voudrais’ means ‘I would like’.
20967.m: With ‘je voudrais’ you politely say what you would like in French.

20968.q: What does the French verb ‘venir’ mean?
20968.e: ‘Venir’ means to come, for example ‘Tu viens avec moi ?’ (Are you coming with me?). To stay is ‘rester’ and to wait ‘attendre’.
20968.m: The French verb ‘venir’ means to come.

20969.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘He ___ to school every day.’?
20969.e: With he, she and it the verb gets an -s in the simple present; with ‘go’ it is ‘goes’.
20969.m: With ‘he’, ‘she’ and ‘it’ the verb gets an -s in the present tense.

20970.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Je ___ français.’?
20970.e: For verbs ending in -er, the form with ‘je’ ends in -e, so ‘je parle’.
20970.m: For -er verbs the form with ‘je’ ends in -e.

20971.q: Which verb form fits the question ‘Tu ___ un frère ?’?
20971.e: In the present tense ‘avoir’ goes j'ai, tu as, il a. So ‘tu’ needs ‘as’.

20972.q: Which verb form fits the question ‘Vous ___ suisses ?’?
20972.e: With ‘vous’ the verb ‘être’ is ‘êtes’. ‘Sommes’ goes with ‘nous’.

20973.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘I ___ hungry.’?
20973.e: With ‘I’ the verb ‘to be’ is always ‘am’.

20974.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Ils ___ au cinéma.’?
20974.e: With ‘ils’ the verb ‘aller’ is ‘vont’. ‘Je vais’, ‘il va’ and ‘vous allez’ are other persons.

20975.q: Which word is missing in the sentence ‘Look! It ___ raining.’?
20975.e: For something happening right now you use the present progressive, with ‘is’ for ‘it’.
20975.m: What is happening right now goes in the present progressive in English.

20976.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Nous ___ nos devoirs.’?

20977.q: What is the simple past of ‘go’?
20977.e: ‘Go’ is irregular; its simple past is ‘went’. ‘Gone’ is the past participle.

20978.q: What is the simple past of ‘buy’?
20978.e: ‘Buy’ is irregular and its simple past is ‘bought’. ‘Brought’ belongs to ‘bring’.

20979.q: Which verb form fits the sentence ‘Yesterday I ___ a film.’?
20979.e: ‘Yesterday’ needs the simple past. With regular verbs you add -ed.
20979.m: Regular verbs form the simple past with -ed.

20980.q: Which auxiliary verb fits the sentence ‘J'___ mangé une pomme.’?
20980.e: Most verbs form the passé composé with ‘avoir’. With ‘je’ it is ‘j'ai’.
20980.m: Most verbs form the passé composé with ‘avoir’.

20981.q: Which auxiliary verb fits the sentence ‘Elle ___ allée à Genève.’?
20981.e: ‘Aller’ forms the passé composé with ‘être’. That is why it is ‘elle est allée’.
20981.m: The verb ‘aller’ forms the passé composé with ‘être’.

20982.q: Which signal word typically shows the simple past in English?
20982.e: ‘Yesterday’ points to a finished action in the past.
20982.m: With ‘yesterday’ or ‘last week’ English usually uses the simple past.

20983.q: Which short answer fits ‘Did you see the match?’?
20983.e: The question starts with ‘did’, so the short answer uses ‘did’.
20983.m: In a short answer you repeat the auxiliary verb of the question.

20984.q: What is the past participle of ‘faire’?
20984.e: ‘Faire’ is irregular; the participle is ‘fait’, as in ‘j'ai fait’.

20985.q: What is the past participle of ‘voir’?
20985.e: ‘Voir’ is irregular; the participle is ‘vu’, for example ‘j'ai vu’.

20986.q: What time is ‘It's half past seven’?
20986.e: ‘Half past seven’ means half an hour after seven, so 7.30. In German you say ‘halb acht’, half an hour before eight.
20986.m: With ‘half past’ you add half an hour to the hour.

20987.q: What time is ‘Il est huit heures et quart’?
20987.e: ‘Et quart’ means and a quarter, so a quarter of an hour after eight.
20987.m: With ‘et quart’ you add a quarter of an hour in French.

20988.e: ‘To’ means before. A quarter to nine is 8.45.
20988.m: With ‘quarter to’ there is still a quarter of an hour until the full hour.

20989.e: ‘Midi’ is midday, so 12 o'clock. Midnight is ‘minuit’.
20989.m: At 12 o'clock in the day it is ‘midi’ in French.

20990.q: What time is ‘Il est trois heures moins le quart’?
20990.e: ‘Moins le quart’ means minus a quarter. Three o'clock minus 15 minutes makes 2.45.
20990.m: With ‘moins le quart’ you take away a quarter of an hour.

20991.q: How do you say 10.20 in English?
20991.e: Up to the half hour you say how many minutes ‘past’ the hour it is. 20 minutes after ten is ‘twenty past ten’.
20991.m: Up to the half hour you use ‘past’ in English.

20992.q: What does the English abbreviation ‘a.m.’ mean with a time?
20992.e: ‘A.m.’ comes from the Latin ‘ante meridiem’ and means before noon. After noon is ‘p.m.’.
20992.m: In English, times in the morning are marked ‘a.m.’.

20993.q: What time is ‘Il est dix heures et demie’?
20993.e: ‘Et demie’ means and a half, so half an hour after ten.
20993.m: With ‘et demie’ you add half an hour in French.

20994.e: ‘Abbiegen’ means to turn and ‘links’ means left. Right is ‘rechts’.

20995.e: ‘Tout droit’ means straight on. ‘Allez’ here is the polite command with ‘vous’.
20995.m: If you go ‘tout droit’, you go straight on.

20996.e: ‘À droite’ means to the right. ‘Droite’ here means the right-hand side.
20996.m: If you go ‘à droite’, you turn right.

20997.e: ‘Next to’ is ‘neben’ in German. ‘Hinter’ means behind and ‘gegenüber’ opposite.

20998.q: What does the French phrase ‘en face de’ mean?
20998.e: ‘En face de’ means opposite. Next to is ‘à côté de’.
20998.m: What is ‘en face de’ something is opposite it.

20999.q: Which is the correct way to ask the way to the station in English?
a: How do I get to the station?
Where do I get the station?
What is the way at station?
20999.e: The correct question is ‘How do I get to the station?’. ‘To get to’ means to reach a place.
20999.m: You ask the way in English with ‘How do I get to ...?’.

21000.q: What does ‘la deuxième rue à gauche’ mean?
a: the second street on the left
the second street on the right
the first street on the left
the second crossroads on the right
21000.e: ‘Deuxième’ means second, ‘rue’ street and ‘à gauche’ on the left.

21001.e: ‘Traffic lights’ are the light signals on the road, in German ‘Ampel’. A crossroads is ‘Kreuzung’.

21002.q: What does ‘Je voudrais un croissant, s'il vous plaît.’ mean?
a: Do you have any croissants left?
21002.e: ‘Je voudrais’ means I would like, and ‘s'il vous plaît’ means please. In Switzerland a croissant is often called a ‘Gipfeli’.
21002.m: At the bakery you order politely with ‘Je voudrais ..., s'il vous plaît’.

21004.q: What does ‘L'addition, s'il vous plaît.’ mean in a restaurant?
21004.e: In a restaurant ‘l'addition’ is the bill. The menu is ‘la carte’.
21004.m: To pay, you ask for ‘l'addition’ in French.

21005.q: What is the polite reply to ‘Thank you!’ in English?
21005.e: ‘You're welcome’ is the polite reply. You use ‘Excuse me’ to get someone's attention.

21006.q: When do you say ‘Enchanté’ in French?
21006.e: ‘Enchanté’ means pleased to meet you and is said when you meet someone for the first time. Women write ‘enchantée’.
21006.m: When you meet someone, you say ‘Enchanté’ in French.

21007.q: What do you say in English when someone sneezes?
21007.e: After a sneeze you say ‘Bless you!’, like ‘Gesundheit!’ in German.
21007.m: When someone sneezes, you say ‘Bless you!’ in English.

21008.e: ‘Bientôt’ means soon. You say it to someone you will see again soon.
21008.m: With ‘À bientôt’ you say ‘see you soon’ in French.

21010.m: To apologise in French, you say ‘Je suis désolé’.

21029.q: What is the plural of the French noun ‘le cheval’?
21029.e: Most nouns ending in ‘-al’ form their plural with ‘-aux’. Exceptions include ‘bals’, ‘festivals’ and ‘carnavals’.
21029.m: Nouns ending in ‘-al’ usually end in ‘-aux’ in the plural.

21095.q: Which side of the road do people drive on in Great Britain?
21095.e: In the United Kingdom and Ireland, traffic drives on the left. In Switzerland and almost all of mainland Europe, people drive on the right.
21095.m: In Great Britain, traffic drives on the left.

a: So that everyone looks the same
So that there are no breaks
21111.e: Rules say what is allowed and what is not. That way everyone knows what to stick to, and there are fewer arguments.
21111.m: Rules help everyone get on well together.

21112.q: Who usually makes the rules in a school class?
21112.e: The teacher sets the class rules, often together with the children. When everyone has a say, everyone sticks to them better.
21112.m: Good class rules are often made together.

21113.q: What often happens when someone breaks a rule of a game?
21113.e: When someone doesn't stick to the rules, the others feel they are being treated unfairly. That is why there is often an argument.
21113.m: Sticking to the rules keeps a game peaceful.

21114.q: Which rule for speaking applies in many classrooms?
a: Put your hand up and wait
21114.e: If you want to say something, you put your hand up and wait until it's your turn. That way everyone can listen to each other.
21114.m: Putting your hand up lets others have their say too.

21115.e: Rules are not fixed for ever. If a rule no longer fits, you can change it together.

a: Rules for a block of flats
A building plan for a house
21116.e: House rules say what applies in a building with many flats. They say, for example, when quiet time is.
21116.m: House rules help neighbours live well together.

21117.q: What does ‘quiet time’ mean in a block of flats?
21117.e: During quiet time, for example at night, you should not make any noise. That way everyone can rest and sleep.
21117.m: During quiet time we are considerate of the neighbours.

21118.q: Why are there rules in football?
21118.e: In football the same rules apply to both teams. That way no team has an unfair advantage.
21118.m: The same rules for everyone make a game fair.

21119.q: Who makes sure that laws are obeyed?
21119.e: The police keep people safe and check that the laws are obeyed. They also help when someone is in trouble.
21119.m: The police protect us and make sure laws are obeyed.

21120.q: Who decides in court whether someone has broken a law?
21120.e: Judges work in court. They listen to everyone and then decide fairly.

21121.q: What does the law say about cycling at night?
a: You must not wear a helmet
21121.e: If you ride a bike at night, you must have lights at the front and back. That way others can see you.
21121.m: With lights on my bike, I can be seen well at night.

21122.q: Where can pedestrians walk safely in town?
a: In the middle of the road
21122.e: The pavement is there for pedestrians. They are protected from cars there.
21122.m: On foot, I walk on the pavement.

21123.q: What must cars do at a zebra crossing when someone wants to cross the road?
21123.e: The road traffic law says that vehicles must give way to pedestrians at zebra crossings. Even so, children should wait until the car has stopped.
21123.m: At a zebra crossing, I wait until the cars have stopped.

21124.q: What is the most important law in Switzerland called?
21124.e: The Federal Constitution is the highest law in Switzerland. All other laws have to fit with it.
21124.m: The Federal Constitution is Switzerland's most important law.

21125.q: Up to what age must children in Switzerland go to school?
21125.e: In Switzerland school is compulsory. It usually lasts 11 years, including nursery school, so up to about the age of 15.
21125.m: In Switzerland school is compulsory for all children.

21126.e: A right is something you are entitled to. For example, every child has the right to go to school.
21126.m: A right is something I am entitled to.

21127.e: A duty is a task you have to carry out. For example, children have to go to school.
21127.m: A duty is a task I have to carry out.

21128.e: Homework is one of the duties of schoolchildren. It helps them practise what they have learned.
21128.m: Homework is a duty of schoolchildren.

21129.q: What duty do adults who earn money have?
21129.e: If you are an adult and earn money, you must pay taxes. The money is used, for example, to build schools and roads.
21129.m: With taxes we pay for schools and roads together.

21130.q: What is one of the duties at home?
21130.e: In a family everyone helps. Children can also help with tidying up or laying the table.
21130.m: At home, everyone helps a little.

21131.e: If you have rights, you also have duties. For example, if you are allowed to join in a game, you also have to stick to the rules.

21132.e: A community is people who have something in common and stick together. It can be a family, a class or a club.
21132.m: In a community, people stick together.

21133.q: Which community do almost all children know first?
21133.e: For most children, the family is the first community. That's where you learn to share and help each other.
21133.m: The family is often a child's first community.

a: A group with the same hobby
21134.e: In a club, people with the same interest meet, for example football, music or gymnastics. There are lots of clubs in Switzerland.
21134.m: In a club, people share a hobby.

21135.q: What do you call help that you give freely and without pay?
21135.e: Many people help as volunteers, for example as coaches in a club. They don't get paid for it.
21135.m: Volunteers help others without getting money for it.

21136.e: When people help each other, everyone feels good. That's how a community becomes strong.
21136.m: Helping others makes the community stronger.

21137.q: What is a community of children who go to school together called?
21137.e: The children in a school class learn together every day. They are a community.
21137.m: My school class is a community.

a: A class meeting to talk things over
A party at the end of school
21138.e: In the class council, the children regularly talk about problems and ideas. Together they look for solutions.
21138.m: In the class council, all the children have a say.

21139.q: What do you do at a neighbourhood party?
21139.e: At a neighbourhood party, the people from the area come together. That way you get to know each other better.
21139.m: At a neighbourhood party, neighbours get to know each other.

21140.e: If you are considerate, you make sure others are all right too. For example, you are quiet when someone is asleep.
21140.m: Being considerate means thinking of others too.

21141.q: What is a good solution in an argument?
21141.e: In an argument it helps to talk to each other calmly. That way you can understand how the other person feels.
21141.m: An argument is best solved by talking.

21142.q: What do you say when you have hurt someone?
21142.e: By saying sorry you show that you regret it. That helps to make peace again.
21142.m: An honest apology helps to make up.

21143.e: Respect means treating other people well, even if they are different. Every person is valuable.
21143.m: I treat other people with respect.

21144.e: Rubbish belongs in the bin or in the recycling. That way our surroundings stay clean for everyone.
21144.m: I throw rubbish in the bin.

21145.q: What do you do when a new child joins the class?
a: Welcome them in a friendly way
21145.e: A new child doesn't know anyone yet. If you are friendly, they soon feel at home.
21145.m: I welcome new children in a friendly way.

a: When someone is picked on again and again
21146.e: In bullying, someone is picked on or left out over a long time. If you notice it, you should get help from an adult.
21146.m: If someone is being bullied, I get help.

21147.e: Fair means just. If you are fair, you treat everyone equally and stick to the rules.
21147.m: Being fair means treating everyone justly.

21148.q: A cake is shared among four children. What is fair?
21148.e: If four children get the same amount, that is fair. Each one then gets a quarter of the cake.
21148.m: When sharing, every child gets the same amount.

21149.q: What is fair behaviour in sport called?
21149.e: Fair play means sticking to the rules and respecting your opponent. Even when you lose, you congratulate fairly.
21149.m: Fair play means playing decently in sport.

21150.e: If you cheat, you secretly give yourself an advantage. That is unfair to the others.
21150.m: Cheating is unfair to the others.

21151.q: What do you do when you have lost a game?
21151.e: A good loser congratulates the winner. Next time you might win yourself.
21151.m: I stay fair even when I lose.

21152.q: How can you fairly decide who starts?
21152.e: With a dice every child has the same chance. Luck decides, not strength.
21152.m: A dice gives everyone the same chance.

21153.q: What is fair when everyone wants to play with the same toy?
21153.e: If you take turns, every child gets a go. That way nobody is left out.
21153.m: When taking turns, everyone gets a go.

21154.q: Who makes sure everyone plays fairly in a football match?
21154.e: The referee knows the rules exactly. He blows the whistle when someone commits a foul.
21154.m: The referee makes sure the game is fair.

21155.q: What do you do in a vote?
21155.e: In a vote, people decide on a question. They can say Yes or No.
21155.m: In a vote I say Yes or No.

21156.q: How do you often vote in class?
21156.e: In class the children raise their hand if they are in favour. Then the hands are counted.
21156.m: In class we often vote by raising our hands.

21157.q: What usually applies after a vote?
21157.e: In a vote, the side with the most votes wins. This is called the majority.
21157.m: After a vote, what the majority wants applies.

21158.q: In a class, 14 children want to go to the zoo and 8 children to the museum. Where does the trip go?
21158.e: 14 children voted for the zoo, only 8 for the museum. The majority chose the zoo.
21158.m: The side with more votes wins.

21159.q: How often a year are there normally federal voting days in Switzerland?
21159.e: In Switzerland there are normally four dates a year for federal votes. Often several questions are voted on the same day.
21159.m: In Switzerland people vote several times a year.

21160.q: On which day of the week are votes held in Switzerland?
21160.e: Voting days in Switzerland are always on a Sunday. But many people vote earlier by post.
21160.m: In Switzerland, voting day is a Sunday.

21161.q: How can many people in Switzerland vote without going to a polling station?
21161.e: The voting papers arrive at home. You can fill in the ballot paper and send it back by post.
21161.m: Many people in Switzerland vote by post.

21162.q: What is secret in a vote?
21162.e: Nobody has to say whether they voted Yes or No. This is called the secret ballot.
21162.m: How I vote can stay secret.

21163.q: What do you do in an election?
21163.e: In an election you decide which people should take on a task. For example, you elect politicians.
21163.m: In an election we decide who takes on a task.

21164.q: Whom can a school class often elect?
21164.e: Many classes elect a class representative. This person speaks for the class.
21164.m: The class representative speaks for the class.

21165.q: What is the difference between an election and a vote?
a: Nobody may take part in elections
21165.e: In an election you decide about people. In a vote you decide about an issue.
21165.m: In elections we decide about people.

21166.q: Since which year have women in Switzerland been allowed to vote and elect at federal level?
21166.e: Since 1971, women in Switzerland have had the right to vote and elect at federal level. Before that, only men could take part.
21166.m: Since 1971, women in Switzerland have been allowed to vote and elect.

21167.q: What is the person called who stands in an election?
21167.e: If you want to be elected, you stand as a candidate. The voters then decide.
21167.m: Someone who wants to be elected is a candidate.

21168.e: Democracy means ‘rule by the people’. In a democracy, people are allowed to help decide.
21168.m: In a democracy, the people have a say.

21169.e: Switzerland is a democracy. The voters elect their representatives and vote on issues.

21170.q: What is it called when the people vote directly on issues?
21170.e: In Switzerland the people often decide on questions themselves. This is called direct democracy.
21170.m: In direct democracy, the people vote themselves.

21171.q: What are you allowed to do in a democracy?
21171.e: In a democracy you may say what you think freely. But you should respect others while doing so.
21171.m: In a democracy I may say what I think.

21172.q: Which language does the word ‘democracy’ come from?
21172.e: The word democracy comes from ancient Greek. ‘Demos’ means people.
21172.m: The word democracy comes from Greek.

21173.q: Who often has the most power in a monarchy?
21173.e: In a monarchy, a king or a queen is at the top. In a democracy, on the other hand, the people have the power.
21173.m: In a monarchy, a king or a queen is at the top.

21174.e: With a popular initiative, people can make a proposal for the Federal Constitution. It needs 100,000 signatures.
21174.m: With a popular initiative, the people can propose something.

21175.q: What is important in a democracy, even if you have lost?
21175.e: In a democracy, the majority's decision applies. Even if you have lost, you accept the result and can try again later.
21175.m: I accept the result of a vote.

21176.q: In many municipalities, who looks after the village school?
21176.e: The municipalities are often responsible for primary school. They build school buildings and employ teachers.
21176.m: The municipality often looks after the primary school.

21177.q: What is the place where the municipality works called?
21177.e: The municipal administration works in the municipal office building. You can report a house move there, for example.
21177.m: The municipal administration works in the municipal office building.

21178.q: In many municipalities, what is the person called who leads the municipality?
21178.e: The municipal president leads the municipality. In some towns the title is town president.
21178.m: A municipal president leads the municipality.

21179.e: At the municipal assembly, the voters of a municipality meet. There they decide on matters in the village.
21179.m: At the municipal assembly, voters help decide.

21180.q: Roughly how many municipalities does Switzerland have (as of 2026)?
21180.e: At the start of 2026, Switzerland had about 2100 municipalities. Because municipalities merge, there are fewer over time.

21181.q: What does a municipality often build and look after for children?
21181.e: Many municipalities build playgrounds and keep them clean. Children can play safely there.
21181.m: The municipality often builds playgrounds for children.

21182.q: Who usually collects the rubbish in the municipality?
21182.e: The municipality organises the bin collection. It regularly picks up the rubbish bags.
21182.m: The bin collection service picks up our rubbish.

21183.e: Every canton has its own coat of arms. You can see it, for example, on flags and number plates.
21183.m: Every canton has its own coat of arms.

21184.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of Bern?
21184.e: The Bern coat of arms shows a black bear. The bear is the symbol of Bern.
21184.m: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern.

21185.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the canton of the Grisons?
21185.e: Among other things, the coat of arms of the Grisons shows an ibex. The ibex lives in the mountains of the Grisons.
21185.m: The ibex is on the coat of arms of the Grisons.

a: A vote in the open air
21186.e: At the Landsgemeinde, people vote outdoors in a square by raising their hands. It still exists today in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
21186.m: At the Landsgemeinde, people vote outdoors.

21187.q: In many cantons, what is the government of a canton called?
21187.e: In many cantons the government is called the Government Council. In some cantons it is called the Council of State.
21187.m: Many cantons are led by a Government Council.

21188.q: What is the federal city of Switzerland called?
21188.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The government and parliament work there.
21188.m: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.

21189.q: In which building does the Swiss parliament meet?
21189.e: Parliament meets in the Federal Palace. The members of parliament meet there several times a year for sessions.
21189.m: The Swiss parliament meets in the Federal Palace.

21190.q: When is the Swiss National Day?
21190.e: On 1 August Switzerland celebrates its birthday. Many people celebrate with paper lanterns and bonfires on the hills.
21190.m: Swiss National Day is on 1 August.

21191.q: What are the two chambers of the Swiss parliament called?
a: National Council and Council of States
Grand Council and Council of States
Federal Council and Federal Supreme Court
21191.e: The Swiss parliament is made up of the National Council and the Council of States. Together they are called the Federal Assembly.
21191.m: Parliament is made up of the National Council and the Council of States.

21192.q: What is the currency of Switzerland called?
21192.e: In Switzerland you pay with francs and centimes (Rappen). One franc has 100 centimes.
21192.m: In Switzerland you pay with francs.

21193.e: Children's rights are special rights for all children in the world. They are meant to protect and support children.
21193.m: Children's rights apply to all children in the world.

21195.q: On which day is the International Day of Children's Rights?
21195.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted on 20 November 1989. That is why children's rights are celebrated on this day.
21195.m: Children's Rights Day is on 20 November.

21196.q: Which right do all children have?
a: The right to a mobile phone
21196.e: Children have the right to play, free time and rest. Playing is important so that children grow up healthy.
21196.m: All children have the right to play.

21197.q: Which right protects children from violence?
21197.e: No child may be hit or treated badly. Children have the right to be protected from violence.
21197.m: Every child has the right to be protected from violence.

21198.q: Which phone number can children in Switzerland call when they are worried?
21198.e: 147 is Pro Juventute's helpline for children and young people. The call is free.
21198.m: When they are worried, children can call 147.

21199.q: Which right means that children may have a say in important things?
21199.e: Children may give their opinion when it is about them. Adults should listen to them and take their opinion seriously.
21199.m: Children may have a say in things that affect them.

21200.q: Which language does the word ‘democracy’ come from?
21200.e: ‘Democracy’ is made up of the Greek words ‘demos’ (people) and ‘kratos’ (rule). So it means ‘rule by the people’.
21200.m: Democracy literally means rule by the people.

21201.q: In which ancient city did an early form of democracy develop about 2500 years ago?
21201.e: In the 5th century BC, the free male citizens of Athens decided together in the people's assembly. But women, slaves and foreigners were not allowed to take part.
21201.m: Athenian democracy is seen as an early model of democracy.

21202.q: What do you call a democracy in which the people can vote on issues themselves?
21202.e: In a direct democracy, the voters decide on laws and changes to the constitution themselves. Switzerland combines direct democracy with an elected parliament.
21202.m: In direct democracy, the people vote on issues themselves.

21203.q: In which two cantons is there still a Landsgemeinde at cantonal level today (as of 2026)?
21203.e: At the Landsgemeinde, voters gather in the open air and vote by raising their hands. Other cantons such as Nidwalden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden or Obwalden abolished it in the 1990s.
21203.m: Only Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden still hold a cantonal Landsgemeinde.

21204.q: Which canton had to be forced by the Federal Supreme Court in 1990 to give women the vote at cantonal level?
21204.e: The Landsgemeinde of Appenzell Innerrhoden rejected votes for women several times. Only a ruling by the Federal Supreme Court in November 1990 brought it in there.
21204.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden was the last canton to give women the cantonal vote.

21205.q: From what age can you vote and elect at federal level in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
21205.e: Since a popular vote in 1991, the voting age at federal level has been 18. Before that it was 20.
21205.m: In Switzerland you can vote and elect at federal level from 18.

21206.q: How many seats does the Council of States have?
21206.e: 20 cantons have two seats each; the six cantons of Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden have one each. That makes 40 + 6 = 46 seats.
21206.m: The Council of States represents the cantons and has 46 members.

21207.q: How many members does the United Federal Assembly have when both chambers meet together?
21207.e: When the National Council and the Council of States meet together, all members of both chambers sit together in the National Council chamber. The United Federal Assembly elects, for example, the judges of the Federal Supreme Court.
21207.m: The United Federal Assembly has 246 members.

21208.q: How many ordinary sessions does the federal parliament hold each year?
21208.e: Parliament meets in spring, summer, autumn and winter for an ordinary session of three weeks each. If needed, there are also special sessions.
21208.m: The federal parliament meets in four ordinary sessions every year.

21209.q: Why is the Swiss federal parliament called a ‘militia parliament’?
a: Most members also have another job
The members are chosen by the army
It only meets in times of crisis
The members work completely without pay
21209.e: Members of parliament usually do their political work alongside their actual job. They are paid for it, but they are not full-time professional politicians.
21209.m: In a militia parliament, politics is a part-time job for most members.

21210.q: What is a group of members of the same party, or of like-minded parties, in the federal parliament called?
21210.e: A parliamentary group needs at least five members from one of the two chambers. Only parliamentary groups may send members to the committees.
21210.m: Members with similar aims join together in a parliamentary group.

21211.q: What does a new federal law need in parliament to be passed?
a: Only the approval of the National Council
Only the approval of the Council of States
The approval of the Federal Supreme Court
21211.e: In Switzerland the National Council and the Council of States have equal rights. A law is only passed if both chambers accept the same text.
21211.m: A federal law needs the approval of the National Council and the Council of States.

21212.q: What is the government of a canton called in most German-speaking Swiss cantons?
21212.e: The Regierungsrat is the executive of a canton and is elected directly by the people. In French-speaking Switzerland the cantonal government is usually called the ‘Conseil d'Etat’ (Council of State).
21212.m: In most German-speaking cantons, the Regierungsrat governs.

21213.q: What is the main task of a government as the executive?
a: Carrying out laws and running the state
Changing the constitution on its own
21213.e: The government runs the administration and makes sure the laws that have been passed are carried out. Passing laws and giving judgements are the tasks of other authorities.
21213.m: The government runs the state and carries out the laws.

21214.q: In many German-speaking Swiss municipalities, what is the executive of a municipality called?
21214.e: In many municipalities, a municipal council elected by the people runs the municipality, led by the municipal president. In larger towns the executive is often called the town council.
21214.m: In many municipalities, the municipal council runs things.

21215.q: Who heads the Federal Chancellery, the staff office of the Federal Council?
a: The President of the Federal Supreme Court
21215.e: The Federal Chancellery is headed by the Federal Chancellor; since 2024 this has been Viktor Rossi. He is not a member of the Federal Council, but takes part in its meetings.
21215.m: The Federal Chancellery is headed by the Federal Chancellor.

21216.q: What is the post of head of government in Germany called?
21216.e: In Germany, the Federal Chancellor leads the federal government. The Federal President is head of state and mainly has ceremonial duties.
21216.m: In Germany, the Federal Chancellor leads the government.

21217.q: What is the head of government in the United Kingdom called?
21217.e: In the United Kingdom, the Prime Minister leads the government. The head of state is the King, but he has hardly any political power.
21217.m: In the United Kingdom, the Prime Minister leads the government.

21218.q: Who is both head of state and head of government in the USA?
21218.e: The USA is a presidential democracy. The President is head of state and leads the government at the same time.
21218.m: In the USA, the President combines head of state and head of government in one office.

21220.q: What is the task of the legislature?
21220.e: The legislature is the law-making power. At federal level in Switzerland this is the Federal Assembly, together with the people in votes.
21220.m: The legislature is the law-making power.

21221.q: Which authority is the highest judiciary at federal level in Switzerland?
21221.e: The Federal Supreme Court is the highest court in Switzerland. It decides disputes from all areas of law as the final authority.
21221.m: The Federal Supreme Court is the highest court in Switzerland.

21222.q: In which city does the Federal Supreme Court have its headquarters?
21222.e: The headquarters of the Federal Supreme Court is in Lausanne, and two divisions work in Lucerne. The Federal Criminal Court is in Bellinzona.
21222.m: The Federal Supreme Court has its headquarters in Lausanne.

21223.q: Why may a member of the Federal Council not sit in the National Council at the same time?
a: Because of the separation of powers
Because federal councillors are elected by the people
Because federal councillors must be over 40
21223.e: Those who govern should not keep a check on themselves. That is why members of the government may not belong to parliament or the Federal Supreme Court at the same time.
21223.m: Nobody may sit in the federal government and the federal parliament at the same time.

21224.q: Who is sometimes called the ‘fourth estate’ in the state?
21224.e: Newspapers, radio, television and online media inform the public and keep a check on the powerful through critical reports. That is why they are often called the ‘fourth estate’.
21224.m: As the fourth estate, free media keep a check on the powerful.

21225.q: Which authority is the executive at federal level in Switzerland?
21225.e: According to Article 174 of the Federal Constitution, the Federal Council is the highest governing and executive authority of the Confederation. It is supported by the federal administration.
21225.m: At federal level, the Federal Council is the executive power.

21226.q: For how many years is a member of the Federal Council elected?
21226.e: The term of office is four years. Members can be re-elected as often as they like, and many stay in office for several terms.
21226.m: Federal councillors are elected for four years.

21227.q: Who is President of the Swiss Confederation in 2026?
21227.e: In December 2025 the Federal Assembly elected Guy Parmelin as President of the Confederation for 2026. He was already President in 2021.
21227.m: Guy Parmelin is President of the Confederation in 2026.

21228.q: What does the ‘principle of collegiality’ in the Federal Council mean?
21228.e: The Federal Council decides as a body. Even members who disagreed in the meeting then publicly stand behind the decision.
21228.m: In the Federal Council, all members stand behind joint decisions.

21229.q: What is the name for the sharing of Federal Council seats from 1959 to 2003, with two seats each for the FDP, CVP and SP and one for the SVP?
21229.e: The so-called magic formula stayed unchanged for 44 years. In 2003 the SVP gained a second seat and the CVP lost one.
21229.m: From 1959 to 2003 the magic formula decided the make-up of the Federal Council.

21230.q: Which party was formed in 2021 from the merger of the CVP and the BDP?
21230.e: The Christian Democratic People's Party and the Conservative Democratic Party merged on 1 January 2021. The new party is called The Centre.
21230.m: The Centre was formed in 2021 from the CVP and the BDP.

21231.q: Which of today's Federal Council parties was founded as a national party as early as 1888?
21231.e: The Social Democratic Party of Switzerland was founded in 1888. The national FDP followed in 1894, and the SVP was only formed in 1971.
21231.m: The SP was founded as a national party in 1888.

21232.q: What does the abbreviation ‘GLP’ stand for?
21232.e: The Green Liberal Party of Switzerland was founded at national level in 2007. It combines environmental concerns with liberal economic policy.
21232.m: GLP stands for Green Liberal Party.

21233.q: What is an important task of political parties?
21233.e: Parties bring opinions together, develop political programmes and put up candidates for elections. This way they help people form political opinions.
21233.m: Parties put up candidates and bring political opinions together.

21234.q: What is the Swiss system called in which the large parties are represented together in the government?
21234.e: In Switzerland, the parties with the most voters are represented together on the Federal Council. Instead of government against opposition, broadly supported solutions are sought.
21234.m: Concordance brings the large parties into government together.

21235.q: What do you call a state in which only one party is allowed?
21235.e: In a one-party state there is no real choice in elections. Other parties are banned or have no chance of gaining power.
21235.m: In a one-party state, only one party is allowed.

21236.q: Every how many years is the National Council elected?
21236.e: The National Council's term lasts four years. The last elections were in 2023, the next are in 2027.
21236.m: The National Council is elected every four years.

21237.q: Which electoral system is used to elect the National Council?
21237.e: With proportional representation, seats are shared out in proportion to the votes for the party lists. That way smaller parties are represented too.
21237.m: The National Council is elected by proportional representation.

21238.q: What does ‘panachage’ mean in an election with lists?
a: Putting in a completely blank list
Voting by post instead of at the ballot box
21238.e: With panachage, you write candidates from other party lists onto your list. This way you can vote for people from different parties.
21238.m: Panachage means voting for candidates from different lists.

21239.q: Who elects the members of the Council of States?
21239.e: Today, in all cantons, the voters elect their members of the Council of States directly. Each canton decides on its own electoral system.
21239.m: The voters of each canton elect their members of the Council of States themselves.

a: Nobody may find out whom you voted for
The election date is not revealed
21240.e: Everyone should be able to vote freely, without pressure from others. That is why the casting of votes must stay secret.
21240.m: The secret ballot protects the free choice of every voter.

21241.q: What is the right to be elected to an office yourself called?
a: The right to stand for election
21241.e: The right to vote is the right to choose others. The right to stand for election is the right to be elected yourself.
21241.m: With the right to stand for election, you can be elected yourself.

21242.q: In which month are the Swiss federal elections usually held?
21242.e: The National Council elections and most Council of States elections take place on a Sunday in October. The new parliament then meets in the winter session.
21242.m: The federal elections take place in October.

21243.q: How much time do you have to collect the signatures for a federal popular initiative?
21243.e: The deadline starts when the initiative is published in the Federal Gazette. If not enough signatures are collected within 18 months, the initiative fails.
21243.m: A popular initiative has 18 months to collect signatures.

21244.q: What does a popular initiative need in order to be accepted?
a: A majority of the people and of the cantons
Only a majority of the people
Only a majority of the cantons
The approval of the Federal Council
21244.e: It needs a majority of voters across the whole of Switzerland and a majority of the cantons. This is called the double majority.
21244.m: A popular initiative needs the double majority of the people and the cantons.

21245.q: How many cantonal votes are there in total for the majority of the cantons?
21245.e: 20 cantons each have one full cantonal vote, and six cantons each have half a vote. 20 + 6 × 0.5 = 23 cantonal votes.
21245.m: For the majority of the cantons, there are 23 cantonal votes in total.

21246.q: What is the vote called that must take place whenever the Federal Constitution is changed?
21246.e: Every change to the constitution must be put to the people and the cantons, without anyone having to collect signatures. This also applies to joining certain international organisations.
21246.m: Changes to the constitution always go to a popular vote.

21247.q: How many dates for federal popular votes are usually planned each year?
21247.e: Every year the Federal Council sets four voting Sundays. Several proposals can be voted on at the same time on one date.
21247.m: There are usually four federal voting dates a year.

21248.q: What is a “direct counter-proposal” to a popular initiative?
a: An alternative from parliament to the initiative
A second initiative by the opponents
A ruling by the Federal Supreme Court
A petition to the Federal Council
21248.e: Parliament can set its own constitutional text against an initiative. The people then vote on both proposals and answer a tie-break question.
21248.m: With a counter-proposal, parliament offers an alternative to the initiative.

21249.q: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
21249.e: The declaration was adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris in 1948. It was a response to the crimes of the Second World War.
21249.m: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights dates from 1948.

21250.q: How many articles does the Universal Declaration of Human Rights have?
21250.e: The 30 articles describe rights such as the right to life, freedom, education and freedom of expression. The declaration is not a treaty, but it is seen worldwide as a foundation.
21250.m: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights has 30 articles.

21251.q: What is the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR)?
a: A treaty of European states to protect human rights
A meeting of the Federal Councillors
21251.e: In the ECHR, the member states of the Council of Europe commit to protecting human rights. Switzerland has been part of it since 1974.
21251.m: The ECHR protects human rights in Europe.

21252.q: On which date is International Human Rights Day?
21252.e: On 10 December, people remember the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The Nobel Peace Prize is also awarded on this day.
21252.m: Human Rights Day is celebrated every year on 10 December.

21253.q: In which city is the UN Human Rights Council based?
21253.e: The Human Rights Council was founded in 2006 and meets in the Palais des Nations in Geneva. It regularly reviews the human rights situation in all UN member states.
21253.m: The UN Human Rights Council meets in Geneva.

21254.q: Which principle is stated in the first article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
a: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights
Everyone has the right to their own house
Every state may decide its laws freely
All people must follow the same religion
21254.e: Article 1 stresses that all people are of equal worth. They should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.
21254.m: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.

21255.q: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
21255.e: The UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child in New York. It is the human rights treaty with the most states parties.
21255.m: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in 1989.

21256.q: Up to what age is a person usually considered a child under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
21256.e: Article 1 of the convention defines every person under 18 as a child. Exceptions only apply if a country sets the age of adulthood earlier.
21256.m: For the Convention on the Rights of the Child, everyone under 18 is a child.
