21783.q: How many quavers (eighth notes) last as long as one minim (half note)?
21783.e: A minim lasts two crotchets, and each crotchet is made of two quavers. So 2 times 2 makes 4 quavers.
21783.m: A minim is as long as four quavers.

21784.q: How many different notes does a major scale have?
21784.e: A major scale has seven different degrees. The eighth note is the starting note again, an octave higher.
21784.m: A major scale has seven different notes.

21785.q: Which major scale has no sharps or flats at all?
21785.e: C major is made only of the natural notes C, D, E, F, G, A, B. On a piano you play it with only the white keys.
21785.m: C major needs neither sharps nor flats.

21786.q: Between which degrees of a major scale are the semitone steps?
21786.e: In major the steps go tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. So the semitones are between the 3rd and 4th and the 7th and 8th degrees.
21786.m: In major, the semitones are between the third and fourth and the seventh and eighth degrees.

21787.q: Which minor key is the relative minor of C major?
21787.e: The relative minor key starts a minor third below the major key's starting note. That is why A minor, like C major, has no sharps or flats.
21787.m: Every major key has a minor key with the same key signature.

21788.q: How many semitone steps are there in an octave?
21788.e: If you count all the white and black keys on a piano from C to the next C, you get twelve semitone steps.
21788.m: An octave is divided into twelve semitones.

21789.q: How many different notes does a pentatonic scale have?
21789.e: “Penta” means five in Greek. The pentatonic scale has no semitone steps and is common in folk music all over the world.
21789.m: The pentatonic scale is a scale of five notes.

21790.q: How many sharps are there in the key signature of G major?
21790.e: G major needs an F sharp so that the semitones are in the right place. That is why there is a sharp at the start of every line.
21790.m: G major has one sharp, F sharp.

21791.q: How many crotchet beats are there in a bar of 3/4 time?
21791.e: A bar of 3/4 time has three beats, and each one is a crotchet. You count “one, two, three”.
21791.m: A bar of 3/4 time has three crotchet beats.

21792.q: Which time signature is typical of the waltz?
21792.e: The waltz is a turning dance with an accent on the first of three beats. You count “one, two, three”.
21792.m: The waltz is in three-four time.

21793.q: What is an incomplete bar at the start of a piece of music called?
21793.e: If a piece begins before the first strong beat, it is called an upbeat. The missing beats are usually made up in the last bar.
21793.m: An upbeat is an incomplete bar at the start of a piece.

21794.q: Which time signature is often written with the sign “C”?
21794.e: The sign “C” stands for four-four time, also called common time. A C with a line through it, on the other hand, means cut time (alla breve).
21794.m: The sign C means four-four time.

21795.q: What is the vertical line in sheet music that separates the bars called?
21795.e: The bar line runs vertically through the whole stave. A double bar line marks the end of a section or piece.
21795.m: Bar lines divide music into bars.

21796.q: How many quavers (eighth notes) fit into a bar of 6/8 time?
21796.e: A bar of 6/8 time holds six quavers. You usually feel it as two groups of three quavers.
21796.m: A bar of 6/8 time has room for six quavers.

21797.q: What does the bottom number of a time signature tell you?
a: The note value of one beat
21797.e: The bottom number gives the note value that is counted, for example 4 for crotchets. The top number says how many of them fit in a bar.
21797.m: The bottom number of a time signature gives the note value counted.

21798.q: Which country does reggae music come from?
21798.e: Reggae began in Jamaica in the late 1960s. Bob Marley made it famous around the world.

21799.q: In which country did the tango mainly develop?
21799.e: The tango developed at the end of the 19th century on the Río de la Plata, mainly in Buenos Aires and also in Montevideo (Uruguay).
21799.m: The tango comes from Buenos Aires in Argentina.

21800.q: What is the often melancholy song style from Portugal called?
21800.e: Fado began in Lisbon in the 19th century. It is usually accompanied by guitars and is part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.
21800.m: Fado is a sad song style from Portugal.

21801.q: Which country does the samba come from?
21801.e: The samba developed in Brazil, especially in Rio de Janeiro. It has African roots and shapes the carnival in Rio.

21802.q: Which instrument is typical of Swiss Ländler music?
21802.e: The Schwyzerörgeli is a small accordion and the most important instrument in Ländler music. The clarinet and double bass often play along.
21802.m: The Schwyzerörgeli belongs to Ländler music.

21803.q: What is the singing style in which you switch quickly between chest voice and head voice called?
21803.e: When yodelling, the voice jumps quickly back and forth between the low chest voice and the high head voice. Yodelling is especially common in Switzerland and Austria.
21803.m: When yodelling, you switch between chest voice and head voice.

21804.q: Which electronic dance music began in Chicago in the 1980s?
21804.e: House began in clubs in Chicago and is named after the club “Warehouse”. Techno began at about the same time in Detroit.

21805.q: Which three composers are regarded as the great Viennese classical composers?
21805.e: Joseph Haydn, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and Ludwig van Beethoven all worked in Vienna. They shaped the music of the Classical period especially strongly.
21805.m: Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven are the three Viennese classical composers.

21806.q: Roughly when was the Viennese Classical period?
a: In the late 18th and early 19th century
In the second half of the 19th century
In the first half of the 20th century
21806.e: The heart of the Viennese Classical period lies roughly between 1780 and Beethoven's death in 1827. The Classical period as a whole is usually dated from about 1750 to the early 19th century.
21806.m: The Viennese Classical period flourished in the late 18th and early 19th century.

21807.q: Which composer is often called the “father of the symphony”?
21807.e: Joseph Haydn wrote over a hundred symphonies and developed the form decisively. He is also regarded as the father of the string quartet.
21807.m: Joseph Haydn is regarded as the father of the symphony.

21808.q: How many movements does a classical symphony usually have?
21808.e: A classical symphony usually has four movements: a fast first movement, a slow movement, a minuet and a fast finale.
21808.m: A classical symphony usually has four movements.

21809.q: Which instruments play in a string quartet?
a: Violin, viola, cello and double bass
21809.e: The classical string quartet is made up of a first and second violin, a viola and a cello.
21809.m: A string quartet has two violins, a viola and a cello.

21810.q: What do you call the separate, complete parts of a symphony?
21810.e: A symphony is made up of several movements, each with its own tempo and character. There is a short pause between the movements.
21810.m: A symphony is divided into movements.

21811.q: Which keyboard instrument increasingly replaced the harpsichord in the Classical period?
21811.e: In the fortepiano, little hammers strike the strings; in the harpsichord they are plucked. This lets you play loudly and quietly, hence the name pianoforte.
21811.m: On the fortepiano you can play loudly or quietly depending on your touch.

21812.q: In which city is jazz said to have begun?
21812.e: Jazz began around 1900 in New Orleans in the south of the USA. African American, European and Caribbean musical traditions mixed there.
21812.m: New Orleans is the birthplace of jazz.

21813.q: What do you call making up music on the spot while playing?
21813.e: When improvising, musicians make up the melody in the moment. Improvisation is at the heart of jazz.
21813.m: Improvisation means making up music on the spot while playing.

21814.q: Which jazz trumpeter had the nickname “Satchmo”?
21814.e: Louis Armstrong (1901 to 1971) came from New Orleans. He was famous for his trumpet playing and his gravelly voice.

21815.q: Which jazz style of the 1930s was played by large big bands?
21815.e: In the swing era, big bands such as those of Benny Goodman or Duke Ellington played dance music. Bebop only began in the 1940s.
21815.m: Swing is the jazz of the great big bands.

21816.q: Which musical form, usually with 12 bars, is an important root of jazz?
21816.e: The blues began among African Americans in the south of the USA. The typical blues pattern has twelve bars.
21816.m: The blues pattern usually has twelve bars.

21817.q: Which jazz singer was called the “First Lady of Song”?
21817.e: Ella Fitzgerald (1917 to 1996) was famous for her clear voice and her scat singing. She won several Grammys.
21817.m: Ella Fitzgerald was the First Lady of Song.

21818.q: Which famous music festival has taken place on Lake Geneva since 1967?
21818.e: The Montreux Jazz Festival was founded in 1967 by Claude Nobs. It is one of the best-known music festivals in the world.
21818.m: The Montreux Jazz Festival takes place on Lake Geneva.

21819.q: Which musician was called the “King of Rock and Roll”?
21819.e: Elvis Presley (1935 to 1977) became the biggest star of rock and roll in the 1950s.
21819.m: Elvis Presley was the King of Rock and Roll.

21820.q: Which city did the Beatles come from?
21820.e: The Beatles were formed in Liverpool in 1960. John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr are regarded as one of the most successful bands in history.

21821.q: Which instrument especially shapes the sound of rock music?
21821.e: The electric guitar is played through an amplifier and can sound loud and distorted. Together with bass and drums, it is the core of a rock band.
21821.m: The electric guitar is the typical instrument of rock music.

21822.q: In which decade did rock and roll begin?
21822.e: Rock and roll began in the USA in the early 1950s, growing out of rhythm and blues and country.
21822.m: Rock and roll began in the 1950s.

21823.q: Which Swiss hard rock band from Ticino is named after an Alpine pass?
21823.e: The band was formed in Ticino in the early 1990s and named itself after the Gotthard Pass. It had many number-one albums in Switzerland.
21823.m: The hard rock band Gotthard comes from Ticino.

21824.q: Which British band released the song “Bohemian Rhapsody” in 1975?
21824.e: “Bohemian Rhapsody” came out in 1975 on Queen's album “A Night at the Opera”. The singer was Freddie Mercury.
21824.m: Bohemian Rhapsody is a song by the band Queen.

21825.q: Which style of rock in the 1970s was known for short, fast and raw songs?
21825.e: Punk began in the mid-1970s in New York and London. Bands like the Ramones deliberately played simply, loudly and fast.
21825.m: Punk rock is short, fast and raw.

21826.q: Which singer was called the “King of Pop”?
21826.e: Michael Jackson (1958 to 2009) was one of the most successful musicians ever. His 1982 album “Thriller” is considered the best-selling album in the world.
21826.m: Michael Jackson was the King of Pop.

21827.q: Which word does the name “pop” come from?
21827.e: “Pop” comes from the English word “popular”, meaning well liked by many people. Pop music aims to appeal to a wide audience.

21828.q: In which Swiss city was the first Eurovision Song Contest held in 1956?
21828.e: The first Eurovision Song Contest took place in Lugano on 24 May 1956. It was won by the Swiss singer Lys Assia.
21828.m: The first Eurovision Song Contest took place in Ticino.

21829.q: Who won the Eurovision Song Contest for Switzerland in 2024?
21829.e: Nemo from Biel won the contest in Malmö in 2024 with the song “The Code”. It was Switzerland's third win.
21829.m: Nemo won the Eurovision Song Contest for Switzerland in 2024.

21830.q: In which Swiss city was the 2025 Eurovision Song Contest held?
21830.e: Because Switzerland won in 2024, it hosted the contest in 2025. It took place in May 2025 in the St. Jakobshalle in Basel.
21830.m: The 2025 Eurovision Song Contest took place in Basel.

21831.q: What do you call the part of a song that comes back several times the same?
21831.e: The chorus is repeated between the verses with the same melody and usually the same words. That is why it sticks in your head.
21831.m: The chorus is the part of a song that keeps coming back.

21832.q: What is the best-known music award in the USA called?
21832.e: The Grammy has been awarded by the Recording Academy since 1959. The Oscar is a film award, the Emmy a television award and the Tony a theatre award.
21832.m: The Grammy is the best-known music award in the USA.

21833.q: In which city did hip-hop begin in the 1970s?
21833.e: Hip-hop began in the 1970s in the Bronx, a part of New York. Young people held block parties in the street there.
21833.m: Hip-hop began in the Bronx in New York.

21834.q: Which of these is NOT one of the classic elements of hip-hop?
21834.e: The classic elements of hip-hop are rap, DJing, breakdance and graffiti. Ballet is not one of them.
21834.m: Hip-hop includes rap, DJing, breakdance and graffiti.

21835.q: Which DJ is regarded as the founder of hip-hop because of a party in 1973?
21835.e: DJ Kool Herc played records at a party in the Bronx on 11 August 1973. He repeated the rhythm breaks of records so that people could dance for longer.
21835.m: DJ Kool Herc is regarded as the founder of hip-hop.

21836.q: What is a rapper in hip-hop also called?
21836.e: MC stands for “Master of Ceremonies”. Originally the MC got the crowd going; later the word came to mean rapper.

21837.q: What does a DJ do when “scratching”?
a: Moves the record back and forth
21837.e: When scratching, the DJ moves the record back and forth by hand. This makes a scratching sound.
21837.m: When scratching, a record is moved back and forth by hand.

21838.q: What do you call a section of someone else's recording that is used in a new song?
21838.e: A sample is a short piece of an existing recording, for example a drum rhythm. In hip-hop, samples are often used as the basis for new beats.
21838.m: A sample is a section of someone else's recording.

21839.q: What is the acrobatic hip-hop dance style with moves on the floor called?
21839.e: Breakdance began in the Bronx. Dancers spin on their backs, heads or hands. In Paris in 2024, breaking was part of the Summer Olympics for the first time.
21839.m: Breakdance is the dance of hip-hop.

21840.q: Which is the lowest string instrument in the orchestra?
21840.e: The double bass is the biggest and lowest string instrument. It is played standing or sitting on a high stool.
21840.m: The double bass is the lowest string instrument.

21841.q: Which group of instruments does the flute belong to?
21841.e: The flute is a woodwind instrument, even though it is usually made of metal today. What matters is how the sound is made, not the material.
21841.m: The flute belongs to the woodwind instruments.

21842.q: Which instrument usually gives the note A for tuning in an orchestra?
21842.e: The oboe has a clear, piercing sound that hardly changes in pitch. That is why the other instruments tune to its A.
21842.m: The oboe gives the orchestra its tuning note.

21843.q: What is the person who leads an orchestra called?
21843.e: The conductor uses the baton to show tempo, entries and volume. The leader heads the first violins.

21844.q: Which brass instrument changes pitch with a slide instead of valves?
21844.e: On the trombone you push the slide out or in. This makes the tube longer or shorter and the note lower or higher.
21844.m: The trombone has a slide instead of valves.

21845.q: Which percussion instrument in the orchestra can be tuned to a particular pitch?
21845.e: On the timpani, the drumhead can be tightened or loosened, often with a pedal. This makes a particular note sound.
21845.m: The timpani can be tuned to a note.

21846.q: How many strings does a violin have?
21846.e: The violin has four strings, tuned to G, D, A and E. It is the highest string instrument in the orchestra.

21847.q: In which city is the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande based?
21847.e: The Orchestre de la Suisse Romande was founded in 1918 by Ernest Ansermet. It plays mainly in the Victoria Hall in Geneva.
21847.m: The Orchestre de la Suisse Romande is based in Geneva.

21848.q: In which city was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born?
21848.e: Mozart was born on 27 January 1756 in the Getreidegasse in Salzburg. The house where he was born is now a museum.

21849.q: How old was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart when he died?
21849.e: Mozart lived from January 1756 to December 1791 and died in Vienna aged only 35. Even so, he created over 600 works.
21849.m: Mozart died at the age of 35.

21850.q: In which Mozart opera does the bird-catcher Papageno appear?
21850.e: “The Magic Flute” was first performed in Vienna in 1791. Papageno is a funny bird-catcher in a costume of feathers.
21850.m: Papageno is a character from The Magic Flute.

21851.q: What was the name of Mozart's father, who taught him as a child?
21851.e: Leopold Mozart was a violinist and composer at the court in Salzburg. He travelled all over Europe with his children Wolfgang and Nannerl.
21851.m: Mozart's father Leopold was his first teacher.

21852.q: Which of Mozart's works was unfinished when he died?
21852.e: Mozart was working on a mass for the dead until his death. His pupil Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work.

21853.q: What is the catalogue by which Mozart's works are numbered called?
21853.e: Ludwig Ritter von Köchel put Mozart's works in time order in 1862. That is why they have the abbreviation K (or KV) with a number.
21853.m: Mozart's works are numbered according to the Köchel catalogue.

21854.q: Roughly how old was Mozart when he composed his first little pieces?
21854.e: At about the age of five, Mozart was already writing his first little piano pieces, which his father wrote down. He was regarded as a child prodigy.
21854.m: Mozart was composing even as a small child.

21855.q: In which city was Ludwig van Beethoven born?
21855.e: Beethoven was born in Bonn on the Rhine. As a young man he moved to Vienna and stayed there until his death.

21856.q: In which year was Ludwig van Beethoven born?
21856.e: Beethoven was born in December 1770; the exact date is not known for certain. He was baptised on 17 December 1770.

21857.q: What condition did Beethoven suffer from from his late twenties onwards?
21857.e: Beethoven became more and more hard of hearing and in the end was almost deaf. Even so, he kept on composing, because he heard the music in his head.
21857.m: Beethoven kept composing even when he was almost deaf.

21858.q: How many symphonies did Beethoven complete?
21858.e: Beethoven completed nine symphonies. Especially well known are the 3rd (“Eroica”), the 5th and the 6th (“Pastoral”).

21859.q: Which poem by Friedrich Schiller did Beethoven set to music in the final movement of a symphony?
21859.e: In the last movement of his Symphony No. 9, Beethoven used a choir and solo singers, which was very unusual in a symphony at the time. It was first performed in Vienna in 1824.
21859.m: Beethoven set Schiller's poem Ode to Joy to music.

21860.q: Which official anthem is based on a melody by Beethoven?
21860.e: In 1972 the Council of Europe chose a melody from Beethoven’s 9th Symphony as its anthem. Since 1985 it has also been the anthem of the European Union.
21860.m: The European anthem comes from Beethoven.

21861.q: Which instrument did Beethoven write the famous piece “Für Elise” for?
21861.e: “Für Elise” is a short piano piece that many piano pupils learn. Beethoven was an excellent pianist himself.
21861.m: “Für Elise” is a piano piece by Beethoven.

21862.q: In which town was Johann Sebastian Bach born in 1685?
21862.e: Bach was born on 21 March 1685 in Eisenach in Thuringia. He came from a large family of musicians.

21863.q: In which city was Bach Thomaskantor (cantor of St Thomas) from 1723?
21863.e: From 1723 Bach, as Thomaskantor, directed the church music in Leipzig and the St Thomas Boys Choir. He stayed there until his death in 1750.

21864.q: Which instrument was Bach especially famous for playing during his lifetime?
21864.e: Bach was one of the best organists of his time and also tested new organs. He wrote many works for this instrument.

21865.q: Which period of music does Johann Sebastian Bach belong to?
21865.e: Bach is one of the most important composers of the Baroque. The year of his death, 1750, is often seen as the end of this period.

21866.q: What job did many members of Johann Sebastian Bach’s family have?
21866.e: Over generations the Bach family produced many organists, cantors and town musicians. Several of Johann Sebastian’s sons also became well-known composers.
21866.m: Bach came from a large family of musicians.

21867.q: What is a fugue, like the ones Bach often composed?
a: A piece in which a theme enters in several voices one after another
A song with only one voice
21867.e: In a fugue one voice introduces a theme, then the other voices take it up one after another. Bach was a master of this form.
21867.m: In a fugue a theme travels through several voices.

21868.q: Bach’s music is often polyphonic. What does that mean?
a: Several melodies sound at the same time
21868.e: In polyphonic music several independent melodies run at the same time and still fit together. Bach mastered this art like hardly anyone else.
21868.m: Polyphonic means several melodies sound at the same time.

21869.q: Which period of music followed the Baroque?
21869.e: The order of the great periods is Middle Ages, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, Romantic. The Classical period began around 1750 and lasted into the early 19th century.
21869.m: The Classical period followed the Baroque.

21870.q: What are the syllables do, re, mi, fa, so, la, ti used for?
a: Singing the notes of a scale
21870.e: These syllables are used to sing the steps of a scale. The idea goes back to the monk Guido of Arezzo in the 11th century, who began with ut, re, mi.
21870.m: Do, re, mi are used to sing the scale.

21871.q: What is the single-line Latin church singing of the Middle Ages called?
21871.e: Gregorian chant is sung in a single melodic line without instruments. It is named after Pope Gregory the Great.
21871.m: Gregorian chant is church singing in a single melodic line.

21872.q: Which sound-recording device did Thomas Edison invent in 1877?
21872.e: Edison’s phonograph recorded sound on a cylinder covered with tinfoil. The gramophone with flat records only followed in 1887, from Emile Berliner.
21872.m: The phonograph was the first machine that could record sounds.

21873.q: Which period do Frédéric Chopin and Robert Schumann belong to?
21873.e: The Romantic period began in the early 19th century and shaped music until around 1900. Composers like Chopin and Schumann expressed strong feelings in their music.
21873.m: Chopin and Schumann are Romantic composers.

21874.q: Which 12th-century nun is one of the first female composers known by name?
21874.e: Hildegard of Bingen (1098 to 1179) was an abbess, scholar and composer. Many of her sacred songs have survived.
21874.m: Hildegard of Bingen was composing as early as the Middle Ages.

21875.q: Roughly when did the Baroque period in music begin?
21875.e: The Baroque lasted from about 1600 to 1750. The first operas were written then, for example by Claudio Monteverdi.
21875.m: The Baroque period in music began around 1600.

22149.q: Roughly how high is the men's world record in the high jump?
22149.e: Javier Sotomayor from Cuba jumped 2.45 metres in 1993. That is clearly higher than most people are tall.
22149.m: The high jump world record is 2.45 metres.

22150.q: How many gold medals did Michael Phelps win at the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing?
22150.e: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals in Beijing in 2008. He beat Mark Spitz, who had won seven gold medals at a single Games in 1972.
22150.m: No athlete has won more gold medals at a single Games than Michael Phelps in 2008.

22151.q: Roughly how fast is the women's 100 metres world record?
22151.e: Florence Griffith-Joyner from the USA ran the 100 metres in 10.49 seconds in 1988. Nobody has matched this time to this day (as of 2026).
22151.m: The women's 100 metres world record is about 10.5 seconds.

22152.q: What is warming up before sport for?
a: It prepares the muscles, heart and circulation for the effort
It makes the muscles stronger straight away
22152.e: When you warm up, your body temperature, pulse and blood flow go up. This helps the muscles work better and lowers the risk of injury.
22152.m: Warming up prepares the body for the effort.

22153.q: What is it called when the body recovers after training to a level above its previous performance?
22153.e: After exercise the body recovers and builds up a little more performance than before. This is called supercompensation.
22153.m: Through supercompensation the body becomes fitter after recovery.

22154.q: Using the rule of thumb 220 minus age, roughly what is the maximum heart rate of a 12-year-old?
22154.e: The sum is 220 minus 12, which makes 208. The rule of thumb only gives a rough guide.
22154.m: You can roughly estimate maximum heart rate as 220 minus your age.

22155.q: What is a type of training called in which periods of effort and recovery alternate regularly?
22155.e: In interval training, intense phases are followed by short breaks. This means you can train at high intensity more often.
22155.m: In interval training, effort and rest alternate.

22156.q: Why are rest days important in training?
a: Because the body adapts and gets stronger during recovery
Because muscles only use energy when resting
Because then you can skip the warm-up
Because you get more sore muscles on rest days
22156.e: Improvement happens in the recovery phase after training. Without enough breaks, there is a risk of overtraining.
22156.m: Without enough recovery you will not get better.

22157.q: What are you measuring if you count your pulse in the morning straight after waking up?
22157.e: The resting heart rate is the heart rate when completely at rest. In well-trained endurance athletes it is often lower than in untrained people.
22157.m: A low resting heart rate is often a sign of good endurance.

22158.q: A runner trains three times a week for 40 minutes each time. How many hours is that in four weeks?
22158.e: Each week it is 3 times 40, which equals 120 minutes. In four weeks that makes 480 minutes, so 8 hours.
22158.m: Training time is easy to add up over the weeks.

22159.e: The marathon distance is exactly 42.195 kilometres. This length was fixed in 1921.

22160.q: What does “aerobic” mean when muscles produce energy?
22160.e: During aerobic exercise the muscle gets enough oxygen to produce energy. This is the case when running calmly for a long time.
22160.m: Aerobic exercise happens with enough oxygen.

22161.q: What do you feel when you run very fast and your muscles no longer get enough oxygen?
a: The muscles feel heavy and burn
22161.e: Without enough oxygen the muscle produces energy in an emergency way. This creates lactate, and the muscles tire quickly.
22161.m: If you go too fast, your muscles quickly get tired.

22162.q: Which three disciplines make up a triathlon, in this order?
22162.e: A triathlon starts with swimming, then comes cycling and finally a run. The changeovers count towards the total time.
22162.m: In a triathlon you swim first, then cycle and run at the end.

22163.q: Which part of the blood carries oxygen to the muscles?
22163.e: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen. This is how oxygen gets from the lungs to the muscles.
22163.m: Red blood cells bring oxygen to the muscles.

22164.q: How does the heart change through regular endurance training?
a: It pumps more blood with each beat
It needs more oxygen at rest
22164.e: A trained heart becomes stronger and pumps more blood with each beat. That is why it needs fewer beats at rest.
22164.m: Endurance training makes the heart stronger.

22165.q: What distance do you run in a half marathon?
22165.e: A half marathon is exactly half the marathon distance. 42.195 divided by 2 makes 21.0975 kilometres.
22165.m: A half marathon is half as long as a marathon.

22166.q: What is the ability to develop force against resistance as quickly as possible called, for example when taking off for a jump?
22166.e: You need explosive strength for sprinting, jumping and throwing, for example. The muscle has to build up a lot of force in a short time.
22166.m: Explosive strength is important for jumps and sprints.

22167.q: What is the greatest force a muscle can produce on purpose called?
22167.e: Maximum strength is the highest force you can produce against a resistance. It is important in weightlifting, for example.
22167.m: Maximum strength is the highest force a muscle can produce.

22168.q: What do you mainly train when you do lots of repetitions with a light weight?
22168.e: Lots of repetitions with little weight improve the ability to keep up a force for a long time. This is called strength endurance.
22168.m: Lots of repetitions with little weight train strength endurance.

22169.q: Which muscle bends the arm at the elbow joint?
22169.e: The biceps is at the front of the upper arm and bends the elbow. Its opposite muscle, the triceps, straightens the arm again.
22169.m: The biceps bends the arm and the triceps straightens it.

22170.q: What is a strength exercise called in which you hold a position without moving, for example the forearm plank?
22170.e: In an isometric exercise the muscle tenses without changing its length. The forearm plank is a well-known example.
22170.m: In isometric exercises you hold a position without moving.

22171.q: Which two disciplines are there in Olympic weightlifting?
22171.e: Weightlifting has the snatch and the clean and jerk. In the snatch the bar is lifted over the head in one movement.
22171.m: Olympic weightlifting has the snatch and the clean and jerk.

22172.q: Which muscle group is mainly trained by squats?
22172.e: In a squat it is mainly the thigh and bottom muscles that work. A straight back is important.
22172.m: Squats mainly strengthen the legs and bottom.

22173.q: Why should children and teenagers start strength training with their own body weight?
a: So they learn the right technique and don't overload their joints
Because body weight is heavier than dumbbells
Because muscles only grow from age 20
Because strength training is forbidden for teenagers
22173.e: Exercises with your own body weight train technique and protect growing joints. Extra weight is only added gradually.
22173.m: In strength training, clean technique comes before heavy weight.

22568.q: What colour do you get when you mix red and white?
22568.e: White makes colours lighter. Red turns into a light red, which we call pink.
22568.m: Red with lots of white turns pink.

22569.q: What colour is the sky on a clear day?
22569.e: Sunlight is spread out in the air. Blue light is scattered the most, which is why the sky looks blue.
22569.m: In fine weather the sky is blue.

22570.q: What colour do you get when you mix black and white?
22570.e: Black and white together make grey. With more white, the grey gets lighter.
22570.m: Black and white together make grey.

22571.q: How many colours do people usually count in a rainbow?
22571.e: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops. People usually count seven colours, from red to violet.
22571.m: A rainbow usually has seven colours.

22572.q: How many sides does a square have?
22572.e: A square has four sides. All four sides are the same length.
22572.m: A square has four sides of equal length.

22573.q: How many corners does a hexagon have?
22573.e: A hexagon has six corners. The cells of a honeycomb have this shape.

22574.q: What shape is each face of a dice?
22574.e: A dice has six faces. Each face is a square.
22574.m: Each face of a dice is a square.

22575.q: What do you call a shape that is completely round, like a ball?
22575.e: A sphere is round on all sides. A ball or a marble has this shape.
22575.m: A ball has the shape of a sphere.

22576.q: What shape is a stop sign?
22576.e: The stop sign is a red octagon with eight corners. That way you can recognise it even from behind.
22576.m: The stop sign is a red octagon.

22580.q: How many legs do two dogs have altogether?
22580.e: A dog has 4 legs. Two dogs have 4 + 4 = 8 legs.
22580.m: Two dogs have eight legs altogether.

22582.q: What is a baby cow called?
22582.e: A baby cow is called a calf. A foal is a young horse.
22582.m: A cow's baby is called a calf.

22583.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
22583.e: Beetles are insects. All insects have six legs.
22583.m: Insects such as beetles have six legs.

22584.q: Which animal in the Alps hibernates for a long time in winter?
22584.e: The marmot sleeps for many months in winter in its burrow underground. The ibex and the chamois stay awake in winter.
22584.m: The marmot sleeps through the winter in its burrow.

22585.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
22585.e: Fish take oxygen out of the water with their gills. They use their fins for swimming.

22586.q: Which of these animals lays eggs?
22586.e: Hens are birds and lay eggs. Cows, horses and sheep give birth to live young.

22587.q: Besides water, what does a plant need to grow?
22587.e: Plants need sunlight. With light, water and air they make their own food.
22587.m: Plants need light and water to grow.

22588.q: Which part of a plant is usually in the soil?
22588.e: The root holds the plant firmly in the ground. It also takes up water from the soil.
22588.m: The root holds the plant in the soil.

22589.q: Which tree do acorns grow on?
22589.e: Acorns are the fruit of the oak tree. Squirrels and wild boar love to eat them.
22589.m: Acorns grow on the oak tree.

22590.q: Which flower is a well-known symbol of the Alps?
22590.e: Edelweiss grows high up in the mountains. It has white, felt-like flowers and is protected in Switzerland.
22590.m: Edelweiss is the famous flower of the Alps.

22591.q: Which tree stays green in winter too?
22591.e: The fir tree has needles that it keeps in winter. Beech, oak and maple lose their leaves in autumn.
22591.m: The fir tree stays green even in winter.

22592.q: Which plant has lots of spines and often grows in the desert?
22592.e: The cactus stores water in its thick stem. Its spines protect it from animals.
22592.m: The cactus stores water and has spines.

22593.q: Which country is the city of Paris in?
22593.e: Paris is the capital of France. France is one of Switzerland's neighbours.
22593.m: Paris is the capital of France.

22594.q: In which city do the Swiss Federal Council and Parliament work?
22594.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Palace is there.
22594.m: The Swiss government works in Bern.

22595.q: Which country is a neighbour of Switzerland?
22595.e: Switzerland has five neighbouring countries: Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.
22595.m: Austria is a neighbour of Switzerland.

22596.q: In which country do kangaroos live in the wild?
22596.e: In the wild, kangaroos are found only in Australia and on a few nearby islands.
22596.m: Kangaroos live in the wild in Australia.

22597.q: Which language do people speak in Italy?
22597.e: People in Italy speak Italian. Italian is also spoken in Ticino, a Swiss canton.

22598.q: Which country is the city of Tokyo in?
22598.e: Tokyo is the capital of Japan. Japan is made up of many islands.
22598.m: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

22599.q: What shape is the Swiss national flag?
22599.e: The Swiss national flag is square. Only very few countries have a flag like this, for example the Vatican.

22600.q: What can you see in the middle of the Swiss flag?
22600.e: In the middle of the red Swiss flag there is a white cross. It is the symbol of Switzerland.
22600.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross.

22601.q: Which country has a flag with a red circle on a white background?
22601.e: The red circle on Japan's flag stands for the sun. Japan is also called the Land of the Rising Sun.
22601.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

22602.q: What colours is the flag of Italy?
22602.e: The flag of Italy has three vertical stripes in green, white and red.
22602.m: The Italian flag is green, white and red.

22603.q: Which country has a black, red and gold flag?
22603.e: The flag of Germany has three horizontal stripes in black, red and gold. The flag of Austria is red, white and red.
22603.m: The German flag is black, red and gold.

22604.q: Which flag shows a circle of twelve yellow stars on blue?
22604.e: The flag of Europe is blue with twelve yellow stars in a circle. The number twelve stands for completeness.
22604.m: The flag of Europe has twelve yellow stars in a circle.

22605.q: Who bakes fresh bread every morning?
22605.e: The baker bakes bread, croissants and plaited Swiss loaves. Bakers often start work in the middle of the night.

22606.q: Who brings letters and parcels to our homes?
22606.e: The postman works for the post office. He puts letters and parcels in the letterboxes.
22606.m: The postman brings letters and parcels.

22607.q: How many wheels does a bike have?
22607.e: A bike has two wheels, one at the front and one at the back. A tricycle has three.

22608.e: A train runs on rails. In Switzerland, lots of people travel by train.

22609.q: Which vehicle flies with a big propeller on its roof?
22609.e: A helicopter has a big spinning rotor on top. With it, it can take off straight up and hover in the air.
22609.m: The helicopter flies with a rotor on its roof.

22610.e: A submarine can dive and travel underwater. Its name means ‘under the sea’.

22611.q: What colour are the PostBuses in Switzerland?
22611.e: The PostBuses in Switzerland are yellow. They even go to small mountain villages.

22612.q: What do you call a railway whose cabin travels through the air on a cable?
22612.e: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from a cable. It gets you up a mountain quickly.
22612.m: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from a cable.

22613.q: Which boat is powered by the wind?
22613.e: A sailing boat catches the wind in its sail. That way it moves forward without an engine.
22613.m: The sailing boat moves using the power of the wind.

22614.q: Which vehicle flies all the way into space?
22614.e: A rocket is very powerful and fast. It can fly all the way into space.

22615.e: Cheese is made from milk, for example cow's milk. Switzerland is famous for its cheese.

22616.e: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans. Cocoa grows on trees in warm countries.
22616.m: Chocolate is made from cocoa beans.

22617.q: Which Swiss dish do you eat from a pot of melted cheese?
22617.e: With fondue, you dip pieces of bread into melted cheese using a long fork.
22617.m: With fondue, you dip bread into cheese.

22618.q: Which vegetable is rösti made from?
22618.e: For rösti, you grate potatoes and fry them in a pan until they are crispy.
22618.m: Rösti is made from grated potatoes.

22619.q: Which bread do people in Switzerland often eat for breakfast on Sundays?
22619.e: Zopf is a plaited bread made with butter, milk and flour. Many families eat it on Sundays.
22619.m: On Sundays there is often a Zopf.

22620.e: Bees collect nectar from flowers. They turn it into honey in the beehive.

22621.q: When do people in Switzerland eat their ‘Znüni’?
22621.e: The Znüni is a small snack in the morning, at about nine o'clock. Many children eat it at break time at school.
22621.m: The Znüni is eaten in the morning.

22622.q: In which country are the pyramids of Giza?
22622.e: The pyramids of Giza are in Egypt. They are over 4000 years old.
22622.m: The pyramids of Giza are in Egypt.

22623.q: What is the very long wall in China called?
22623.e: The Great Wall of China is many thousands of kilometres long. It was built a long time ago for protection.
22623.m: The Great Wall of China is very long.

22624.q: Which large statue in New York holds up a torch?
22624.e: The Statue of Liberty stands on a small island in New York harbour. It was a gift from France to the USA.
22624.m: The Statue of Liberty holds up a torch.

22625.q: In which city is there a famous leaning tower?
22625.e: The tower of Pisa in Italy leans because the ground beneath it is soft.
22625.m: The leaning tower is in Pisa.

22626.q: Which mountain is the highest in the world?
22626.e: Mount Everest in the Himalayas is about 8849 metres high. No mountain on Earth is higher.
22626.m: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

22627.q: Which animal is the largest in the world?
22627.e: The blue whale can grow to about 30 metres long. It is the largest animal living on Earth today.
22627.m: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world.

22628.q: Which land animal is the tallest?
22628.e: A giraffe can grow over five metres tall. With its long neck it reaches leaves high up in the trees.
22628.m: The giraffe is the tallest animal on land.

22629.q: Which land animal runs the fastest?
22629.e: For a short time, the cheetah can run at about 100 kilometres per hour. No other land animal is that fast.
22629.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

22630.q: Which ocean is the largest in the world?
22630.e: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean. It is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.
22630.m: The Pacific is the largest ocean.

22632.q: What do you use to brush your teeth?
22632.e: You brush your teeth with a toothbrush and toothpaste. You should do it at least twice a day.
22632.m: You brush your teeth with a toothbrush.

22633.q: What do you use to cut paper?
22633.e: You can cut paper with scissors. You stick it together with glue.

22634.e: A clock shows the hours and minutes. Scales, on the other hand, measure weight.

22635.q: What do you take with you to stay dry in the rain?
22635.e: An umbrella keeps the rain off. That way you stay dry.
22635.m: An umbrella protects you from the rain.

22636.q: What do you use to unlock a front door?
22636.e: You open the lock of the door with a key. Without the right key, the door stays shut.
22636.m: You unlock the door with a key.

22637.q: Where does food stay cool and fresh?
22637.e: It is cold inside the fridge. That is why milk, cheese and meat do not go off so quickly there.
22637.m: Food stays cool in the fridge.

22638.q: What gets wet while it dries?
22638.e: You dry yourself with a towel. It soaks up the water and gets wet itself.
22638.m: A towel gets wet when you dry yourself.

22639.q: What has teeth but cannot bite?
22639.e: A comb has lots of prongs, which are called teeth. But it cannot bite with them.
22639.m: A comb has teeth but does not bite.

22640.q: What has a bed but never sleeps?
22640.e: The ground a river flows along is called a riverbed. But a river cannot sleep.
22640.m: A river has a bed but never sleeps.

22641.q: Anna's mother has three children: Lena, Tim and who else?
22641.e: The question talks about Anna's mother. So Anna herself is the third child.
22641.m: With riddles, you need to read carefully.

22642.q: Which is heavier, a kilo of feathers or a kilo of stones?
22642.e: A kilo always weighs the same. The feathers just take up much more space.
22642.m: A kilo of feathers weighs the same as a kilo of stones.

22643.q: Riddle: Which months have at least 28 days?
22643.e: Every month has at least 28 days. February has 28 or 29 days, the other months have 30 or 31.
22643.m: Every month has at least twenty-eight days.

22644.q: What has four legs but cannot walk?
22644.e: A table usually has four legs. But it just stands still and cannot walk.
22644.m: A table has legs but cannot walk.

22645.q: Which building is the tallest in the world at 828 metres (as of 2026)?
22645.e: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai opened in 2010 and is 828 m tall. The Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia is meant to beat it, but in 2026 it is still being built.
22645.m: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world.

22646.q: Which sprinter has held the 100 metres world record of 9.58 seconds since 2009 (as of 2026)?
22646.e: The Jamaican Usain Bolt ran 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin. Nobody has run faster since.
22646.m: Usain Bolt holds the 100 metres world record with 9.58 seconds.

22647.q: Which time barrier did the Kenyan Sabastian Sawe become the first person to break in an official race, at the 2026 London Marathon?
22647.e: Sabastian Sawe ran 1:59:30 in London in April 2026. That made him the first person to finish under two hours in an official race.
22647.m: Since 2026, the men's marathon world record has been under two hours.

22648.q: Which swimmer won 28 Olympic medals, more than any other athlete (as of 2026)?
22648.e: Michael Phelps from the USA won a total of 28 Olympic medals between 2004 and 2016, 23 of them gold. That is still a record.
22648.m: Michael Phelps is the most successful Olympian of all time.

22649.q: Which tunnel, about 57 km long, is the longest railway tunnel in the world (as of 2026)?
22649.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel opened in 2016 and is about 57 km long. It links Erstfeld in the canton of Uri with Bodio in Ticino.
22649.m: The longest railway tunnel in the world runs under the Gotthard in Switzerland.

22650.q: Which country has the longest bridge in the world, a railway viaduct about 165 km long (as of 2026)?
22650.e: The Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge is a viaduct on the Beijing to Shanghai high-speed line. It is about 165 km long and opened in 2011.
22650.m: The longest bridge in the world is a railway viaduct in China.

22651.q: Which Swiss man, together with Brian Jones, made the first non-stop balloon flight around the world in 1999?
22651.e: In 1999 Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones flew round the Earth in the balloon “Breitling Orbiter 3” in just under 20 days. They had set off from Château-d'Oex in the canton of Vaud.
22651.m: The first non-stop balloon flight round the world started in Switzerland.

22652.q: In which sport has the Cuban Javier Sotomayor held the world record of 2.45 m since 1993?
22652.e: In 1993 in Salamanca, Javier Sotomayor cleared the bar at 2.45 m. In the long jump and triple jump you jump much further, and in the pole vault much higher.
22652.m: The men's high jump world record is 2.45 metres.

22653.q: In which Swiss city did Albert Einstein work at the patent office when he published his special theory of relativity in 1905?
22653.e: Einstein worked at the Federal Office for Intellectual Property in Bern from 1902 to 1909. In 1905 he published several famous papers there.
22653.m: Albert Einstein wrote his most famous papers while working in Bern.

22654.q: Which scientist was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes?
22654.e: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the one in Chemistry in 1911. She studied radioactivity.
22654.m: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

22655.q: Which organisation did Henri Dunant from Geneva found?
22655.e: In 1859 Henri Dunant saw the suffering of the wounded after the Battle of Solferino. He inspired the founding of the Red Cross and received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
22655.m: Henri Dunant from Geneva is the founder of the Red Cross.

22656.q: In which city was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born in 1756?
22656.e: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756. Even as a child he composed music and toured Europe as a child prodigy.
22656.m: Mozart came from Salzburg in Austria.

22657.q: Which composer wrote the 9th Symphony when he was already almost completely deaf?
22657.e: From about the age of 30, Beethoven slowly lost his hearing. Even so, he kept composing, including the 9th Symphony with the “Ode to Joy”.
22657.m: Beethoven composed great works even though he was deaf.

22658.q: Who became the youngest person to win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, at the age of 17?
22658.e: Malala Yousafzai from Pakistan campaigns for girls' right to education. She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at the age of 17.
22658.m: Malala Yousafzai fights for all girls to be allowed to go to school.

22659.q: Who became South Africa's first black president in 1994, after spending 27 years in prison?
22659.e: Nelson Mandela fought against apartheid, the system of racial segregation in South Africa. After his release in 1990 he became president in 1994.
22659.m: Nelson Mandela became a symbol of the fight against racial segregation.

22660.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did the Basel tennis player Roger Federer win?
22660.e: Roger Federer won a total of 20 Grand Slam titles between 2003 and 2018, eight of them at Wimbledon. He retired in 2022.
22660.m: Roger Federer won Wimbledon eight times.

22661.q: Which Swiss author wrote the story of “Heidi”?
22661.e: Johanna Spyri published the first Heidi book in 1880. It has been translated into many languages and is known all over the world.
22661.m: The Heidi stories were written by Johanna Spyri from Zurich.

22662.q: Which Renaissance artist painted the “Mona Lisa” and also drew flying machines?
22662.e: Leonardo da Vinci was a painter, inventor and scientist. The “Mona Lisa” now hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
22662.m: Leonardo da Vinci was both an artist and an inventor.

22663.q: How did Bertrand Piccard and André Borschberg travel round the Earth in 2015 and 2016?
22663.e: The aircraft “Solar Impulse 2” flew around the world using only solar energy. The journey, in several stages, ended in Abu Dhabi in July 2016.
22663.m: Solar Impulse showed that a plane can fly round the world on solar power alone.

22664.q: Which plant gave the Swiss George de Mestral the idea for Velcro?
22664.e: After a walk, burdock burrs were stuck in his dog's fur. Under the microscope, de Mestral saw the tiny hooks and copied them.
22664.m: Velcro is a Swiss invention modelled on nature.

22665.q: Which company from Ibach in the canton of Schwyz makes the famous Swiss Army knife?
22665.e: At the end of 1891, Karl Elsener in Ibach took over making soldiers' knives for the Swiss Army. His workshop became the company Victorinox, which today sells pocket knives all over the world.
22665.m: The famous Swiss Army knife comes from the canton of Schwyz.

22666.q: In which country was milk chocolate invented in 1875?
22666.e: In 1875 Daniel Peter from western Switzerland mixed cocoa and sugar with condensed milk. His friend Henri Nestlé helped him.
22666.m: Daniel Peter made milk chocolate from western Switzerland famous worldwide.

22667.q: At which research centre did Tim Berners-Lee invent the World Wide Web in 1989?
22667.e: Tim Berners-Lee wanted researchers to be able to share their data easily. At CERN near Geneva he developed web pages, links and the first browser for this.
22667.m: The World Wide Web was invented in Switzerland.

22668.q: Who patented the first petrol-powered car in 1886?
22668.e: In 1886 Carl Benz patented his three-wheeled Motorwagen. It is considered the first practical car.
22668.m: The world's first car had only three wheels.

22669.q: Who made the first controlled powered flight in history in 1903?
22669.e: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew their “Flyer” in the USA on 17 December 1903. The first flight lasted only 12 seconds.
22669.m: In 1903 the Wright brothers started the age of the aeroplane.

22670.q: Which forerunner of the bicycle did Karl Drais invent in 1817?
22670.e: The running machine had two wheels but no pedals. You pushed yourself along the ground with your feet.
22670.m: The first two-wheeler had no pedals yet.

22671.q: In which country did people invent paper?
22671.e: People in China already made paper more than 2000 years ago. Around the year 105, the official Cai Lun greatly improved how it was made.
22671.m: Paper is an invention from ancient China.

22672.q: Which invention made Alfred Nobel rich, whose fortune now pays for the Nobel Prizes?
22672.e: The Swede Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867. In his will he decided that prizes should be awarded every year with his money.
22672.m: The Nobel Prizes are paid for from the fortune of the inventor of dynamite.

22673.q: For what occasion did Paris build the Eiffel Tower in 1889?
22673.e: The Eiffel Tower served as the entrance gate to the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. It was actually meant to be pulled down again after 20 years.
22673.m: The Eiffel Tower was originally only meant for an exhibition.

22674.q: In which country is the Inca ruined city of Machu Picchu?
22674.e: Machu Picchu lies high in the Andes of Peru. The Incas built the city in the 15th century.
22674.m: Machu Picchu is the most famous Inca city, in Peru.

22675.q: Why did the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan have the Taj Mahal built in India?
a: As a tomb for his wife
22675.e: Shah Jahan had the white marble building put up for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. It was finished around 1648.
22675.m: The Taj Mahal is a tomb made of white marble.

22676.q: What took place in the Colosseum in ancient Rome?
22676.e: The Colosseum opened in the year 80 and held about 50,000 spectators. Gladiators fought there and there were animal hunts.
22676.m: In ancient Rome, gladiators fought in the Colosseum.

22677.q: What is the name of Europe's highest railway station, at 3454 metres above sea level?
22677.e: The Jungfrau Railway runs through a tunnel in the Eiger and Mönch up to the Jungfraujoch. It was completed in 1912.
22677.m: Europe's highest railway station is in the Bernese Oberland.

22678.q: Which covered wooden bridge with a water tower is the landmark of Lucerne?
22678.e: Chapel Bridge was built in the 14th century and is one of the oldest wooden bridges in Europe. In 1993 much of it burned down and it was rebuilt.
22678.m: Chapel Bridge with its water tower is the landmark of Lucerne.

22679.q: Which lake is the famous Chillon Castle near Montreux on?
22679.e: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in Lake Geneva. It is one of the most visited historic monuments in Switzerland.
22679.m: Chillon Castle stands right on the shore of Lake Geneva.

22680.q: What exactly does the name “Big Ben” in London refer to?
a: The largest bell in the tower
The river next to the tower
22680.e: “Big Ben” is really the nickname of the great bell. Since 2012 the tower itself has been called the “Elizabeth Tower”.
22680.m: Big Ben is really the name of a bell.

22681.q: Which statement about the Great Wall of China is true?
a: You cannot see it from the Moon
It was built in one year
22681.e: The wall is very long, but only a few metres wide. It cannot be seen with the naked eye from the Moon, as astronauts have confirmed.
22681.m: The idea that you can see the Great Wall of China from the Moon is a myth.

22682.q: How high is Mount Everest according to the joint survey by Nepal and China in 2020?
22682.e: In 2020 Nepal and China gave its height as 8848.86 m. That makes Mount Everest the highest mountain on Earth.
22682.m: At almost 8850 metres, Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

22683.q: What is the name of the highest mountain peak in Switzerland?
22683.e: The Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is 4634 m high. It is named after the general and map-maker Guillaume-Henri Dufour.
22683.m: The highest peak in Switzerland is the Dufourspitze.

22684.q: Where is the deepest point of the world's oceans?
22684.e: At its deepest point, the Mariana Trench in the Pacific is almost 11,000 m deep. Mount Everest would fit inside it.
22684.m: The deepest point of the oceans is in the Mariana Trench.

22685.q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth?
22685.e: Blue whales grow over 30 m long and weigh well over 100 tonnes. They are heavier than the largest known dinosaurs.
22685.m: The blue whale is the largest animal of all time.

22687.q: Which kind of tree is “Hyperion”, the tallest known living tree in the world at about 116 m (as of 2026)?
22687.e: Hyperion grows in California and was discovered in 2006. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.
22687.m: The tallest tree in the world is a redwood in California.

22688.q: In which country is Angel Falls, the highest waterfall on Earth at about 979 m?
22688.e: Angel Falls plunges down from a table mountain in Venezuela. It is about 40 times as high as the Rhine Falls.
22688.m: The highest waterfall in the world is in Venezuela.

22689.q: Which glacier is the largest and longest in the Alps?
22689.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier in Valais is about 20 km long. Because of global warming it melts back a little every year.
22689.m: The longest glacier in the Alps is in Valais.

22690.q: Where was the lowest air temperature ever recorded at a weather station, minus 89.2 °C, measured in 1983?
22690.e: The Russian research station Vostok lies at over 3400 m in the interior of Antarctica. A temperature of minus 89.2 °C was measured there on 21 July 1983.
22690.m: The coldest temperature ever measured comes from Antarctica.

22691.q: Which scientist described the law of gravity in the 17th century?
22691.e: Isaac Newton published his law of gravitation in 1687. According to a story, a falling apple gave him the idea.
22691.m: Isaac Newton explained why things fall to the ground.

22692.q: Which medicine did Alexander Fleming discover by chance in a mould in 1928?
22692.e: Fleming noticed that a mould in a dish was killing bacteria. This led to the first antibiotic.

22693.q: What shape of DNA did James Watson and Francis Crick describe in 1953?
22693.e: DNA is made of two strands wound around each other like a twisted rope ladder. Important X-ray images for this came from Rosalind Franklin.
22693.m: DNA has the shape of a twisted ladder.

22694.q: Which astronomer explained in the 16th century that the Earth goes round the Sun?
22694.e: Copernicus published his work in 1543. Before that, most people believed the Earth was at the centre of the universe.
22694.m: Copernicus put the Sun at the centre of our solar system.

22695.q: What did Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discover in 1895?
a: Rays that pass through the body
22695.e: Röntgen discovered rays that make bones inside the body visible. For this he received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
22695.m: With X-rays you can see inside the body.

22696.q: What did Galileo Galilei discover with his telescope in 1610?
22696.e: Galileo saw four bright dots circling Jupiter: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. This showed that not everything goes round the Earth.
22696.m: Galileo was the first to discover moons around another planet.

22697.q: What status was Pluto given in 2006?
22697.e: Pluto, discovered in 1930, had long been counted as the ninth planet. In 2006 the International Astronomical Union decided that it is a dwarf planet.
22697.m: Since 2006 Pluto has not been a planet but a dwarf planet.

22698.q: What did the Geneva astronomers Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz discover in 1995?
a: A new moon of the Earth
22698.e: They found the first planet orbiting a star like the Sun. For this they received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2019.
22698.m: The first exoplanet around a Sun-like star was discovered by researchers from Geneva.

22699.q: Which particle did scientists detect at CERN near Geneva in 2012?
22699.e: Scientists had predicted the Higgs boson back in 1964. They found it in 2012 at CERN's large particle accelerator, the LHC.
22699.m: The Higgs particle was discovered at CERN in 2012.

22700.q: Against which disease did Edward Jenner develop the first vaccination in 1796?
22700.e: Jenner vaccinated a boy with harmless cowpox, after which the boy was protected against dangerous smallpox. Since 1980 smallpox has been considered wiped out worldwide.
22700.m: The first vaccination in history protected against smallpox.

22701.q: What is Archimedes said to have shouted when he discovered buoyancy in the bath?
22701.e: “Eureka” is Greek and means “I have found it”. Archimedes realised that an object in water is pushed up as strongly as the weight of the water it pushes aside.
22701.m: An object in water is pushed upwards by as much as the displaced water weighs.

22702.q: What is burned at the Sechseläuten festival in Zurich to drive away winter?
22702.e: The Böögg is a snowman made of cotton wool and filled with fireworks. The faster its head explodes, the better the summer is supposed to be.
22702.m: At the Sechseläuten, the Böögg is burned in Zurich.

22703.q: At what time does Basel Carnival begin with the Morgestraich?
22703.e: On the Monday after Ash Wednesday, at 4 in the morning, all the lights in Basel's old town go out. Then groups called Cliques set off with lanterns, drums and piccolos.
22703.m: Basel Carnival starts in the middle of the night at four o'clock.

22704.q: What is the Indian festival of lights called, when many oil lamps are lit?
22704.e: Diwali is celebrated in autumn and stands for the victory of light over darkness. It is one of the most important festivals in Hinduism.
22704.m: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.

22705.q: In which country do people celebrate the “Día de los Muertos” with colourful sugar skulls?
22705.e: On the Day of the Dead at the beginning of November, people in Mexico cheerfully remember those who have died. They decorate altars with flowers, photos and food.
22705.m: In Mexico, people remember the dead with a colourful festival.

22706.q: Why does Chinese New Year fall on a different date every year?
a: It is drawn by lot every year
22706.e: The traditional Chinese calendar follows the Moon and the Sun. That is why the New Year festival always falls between 21 January and 20 February.
22706.m: Chinese New Year follows the lunar calendar.

22707.q: What do people throw at each other at the Indian festival of Holi?
22707.e: Holi is a spring festival in India. People throw coloured powder and coloured water at each other.
22707.m: Holi is the festival of colours.

22708.q: What do people throw at each other at the “La Tomatina” festival in the Spanish town of Buñol?
22708.e: Since 1945 a huge tomato fight has taken place in Buñol every year at the end of August. More than 100 tonnes of ripe tomatoes are used.
22708.m: In Buñol in Spain there is a tomato fight every year.

22709.q: What do people in Japan admire during the spring custom of Hanami?
22709.e: At Hanami, families and friends have picnics under blossoming cherry trees. The blossom lasts only about a week.
22709.m: In Japan, Hanami means looking at the cherry blossom.

22710.q: On which date does Switzerland celebrate its national day?
22710.e: 1 August recalls the Federal Charter of 1291. There are bonfires on the hills, paper lanterns and fireworks.
22710.m: Switzerland celebrates its birthday on 1 August.

22711.q: What does the word “Röstigraben” mean in Switzerland?
a: The language border between German and French
A potato field in the Seeland
22711.e: The “Röstigraben” (rösti ditch) is a joking name for the border between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. It often stands for different opinions in votes.
22711.m: The Röstigraben jokingly separates German-speaking Switzerland from the French-speaking part.

22712.q: When do Muslims who observe the month of Ramadan fast?
22712.e: During the fasting month of Ramadan, people do not eat or drink during the day. After sunset they meet to break the fast together.
22712.m: During Ramadan people fast in the daytime and only eat after sunset.

22713.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
22713.e: Two hearts pump blood through the gills, and a third pumps it through the rest of the body. An octopus's blood is also bluish.
22713.m: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

22714.q: Which food stays edible almost forever if it is stored well?
22714.e: Honey contains very little water and lots of sugar, so bacteria can hardly grow in it. Honey thousands of years old has been found in Egyptian tombs.
22714.m: Thanks to its high sugar content, honey almost never goes off.

22715.q: From a botanical point of view, what type of fruit is a banana?
22715.e: In botany, a berry is a fruit whose whole fruit wall is fleshy and which contains the seeds. The banana fits this description.
22715.m: Botanically speaking, the banana is a berry.

22716.q: What is special about the planet Venus?
a: A day lasts longer than a year
22716.e: Venus spins very slowly: one turn takes about 243 Earth days. But it takes only about 225 Earth days to go round the Sun.
22716.m: On Venus a day is longer than a year.

a: Because of colourings in their food
Because they roll in red sand
Because their blood shows through their skin
22717.e: Flamingos eat small shrimps and algae containing red colourings called carotenoids. These are stored in their feathers.
22717.m: Flamingos turn pink because of their food.

22718.q: Why is the Eiffel Tower a few centimetres taller in summer than in winter?
a: Because iron expands when it is warm
Because it is freshly painted in summer
Because the ground swells in summer
Because an aerial is added in summer
22718.e: Metal expands when it gets warm and contracts in the cold. For the iron tower, over 300 m tall, that makes a few centimetres.
22718.m: Most materials expand when they get warm.

22719.q: Which is hotter, a lightning bolt or the surface of the Sun?
22719.e: A lightning bolt briefly heats the air to about 30,000 °C. The surface of the Sun is about 5500 °C.
22719.m: For a moment, lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.

22720.q: Which animals already existed on Earth before the first trees?
22720.e: The first sharks lived over 400 million years ago. The first trees only appeared about 385 million years ago.

22721.q: Which event did the Egyptian queen Cleopatra live closer to in time?
a: The building of the Great Pyramid of Khufu
22721.e: Cleopatra died in 30 BC. The Moon landing came about 2000 years later, but the Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC, about 2530 years before her.
22721.m: Ancient Egypt lasted so long that Cleopatra lived closer to our time than to the building of the pyramids.

22722.q: Which number comes next in the sequence 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
22722.e: Each number is double the one before. 16 times 2 makes 32.
22722.m: In this sequence each number is doubled.

22723.q: Which number comes next in the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...?
22723.e: Each number is the sum of the two before it. 5 plus 8 makes 13.
22723.m: In the Fibonacci sequence you always add the last two numbers.

22724.q: Which number comes next in the sequence 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ...?
22724.e: The gaps are 3, 5, 7 and 9, so they grow by 2 each time. The next gap is 11, and 27 plus 11 makes 38.
22724.m: With number sequences it is worth looking at the gaps between the numbers.

22725.q: A father is 36 years old and his son is 12. In how many years will the father be exactly twice as old as his son?
22725.e: In 12 years the father will be 48 and the son 24. 48 is exactly double 24.
22725.m: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

22726.q: An exercise book and a pen cost 1.10 francs together. The exercise book costs exactly 1 franc more than the pen. How much does the pen cost?
22726.e: The pen costs 5 centimes and the exercise book 1.05 francs. Together that makes 1.10 francs, and the difference is exactly 1 franc.
22726.m: With puzzles, always check your first quick answer.

22727.q: 5 machines make 5 parts in 5 minutes. How long do 100 machines take to make 100 parts?
22727.e: Each machine takes 5 minutes for one part. 100 machines work at the same time and make 100 parts in 5 minutes.
22727.m: If more machines work at the same time, the time per part stays the same.

22728.q: Water lilies double their area every day. After 30 days they cover the whole pond. After how many days did they cover half of it?
22728.e: Because the area doubles every day, the pond had been half covered one day earlier. That means day 29.
22728.m: When something doubles, half is always just one step away from the whole.

22729.q: Anna is taller than Ben. Carla is shorter than Ben. Dario is taller than Anna. Who is the shortest?
22729.e: The order from tallest to shortest is Dario, Anna, Ben, Carla. So Carla is the shortest.
22729.m: With comparison puzzles, it helps to write down the order.

22730.q: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be in 10 days?
22730.e: After 7 days it is Wednesday again. 3 days later, so after 10 days, it is Saturday.
22730.m: Every seven days the same day of the week comes round again.

22731.q: Five children each shake hands with every other child once. How many handshakes are there altogether?
22731.e: Each child shakes hands with 4 others, which gives 5 times 4 equals 20. Because each handshake has been counted twice, you divide by 2 and get 10.
22731.m: With handshakes between people, you may only count each handshake once.

22732.q: A drawer has red and blue socks all mixed up. In the dark, how many socks do you need to take out at least to be sure of two of the same colour?
22732.e: With two socks you might be unlucky and get one red and one blue. But the third sock is sure to be the same colour as one of the two.
22732.m: With two colours, three socks are enough for a sure pair.

22733.q: A train leaves at 14:45 and the journey takes 1 hour and 50 minutes. When does it arrive?
22733.e: 14:45 plus 1 hour makes 15:45. Plus 50 minutes makes 16:35.
22733.m: When working out times, add the hours first and then the minutes.

22734.q: How many months of the year have at least 28 days?
22734.e: Every month has at least 28 days. February has 28 or 29 days, all the others have 30 or 31.
22734.m: Every month of the year has at least 28 days.

22831.q: What does the name Stegosaurus mean?
22831.e: The name means “roof lizard”. People used to think its plates lay flat like tiles on a roof.

22832.q: What did Stegosaurus have at the end of its tail?
22832.e: There were four long spikes at the end of its tail. It could use them to defend itself against attackers.
22832.m: Stegosaurus defended itself with its tail spikes.

22833.e: Stegosaurus was a plant eater. With its small head it ate low-growing plants.

22834.q: How big was the brain of Stegosaurus compared with its body?
22834.e: Stegosaurus was a big animal, but it had a very small brain.

22835.e: Stegosaurus walked on all fours. Its back legs were longer than its front legs.

22836.q: What did the head of Stegosaurus look like?
22836.e: Compared with its body, the head of Stegosaurus was very small and narrow.

22837.q: Did Stegosaurus ever meet Tyrannosaurus rex?
22837.e: Stegosaurus lived long before Tyrannosaurus rex. More than 80 million years lay between them.
22837.m: Stegosaurus and T. rex lived at different times.

22838.q: Where have most Stegosaurus fossils been found?
22838.e: Most finds come from the western USA. There are also some finds in Portugal.
22838.m: Many Stegosaurus fossils are in North America.

22839.q: What were the back plates of Stegosaurus probably for?
22839.e: Scientists think the plates helped other animals recognise it and were used to impress them. It certainly could not fly with them.
22839.m: The back plates were probably for showing off.

22840.q: On which continent did Triceratops live?
22840.e: Triceratops fossils have been found in the western USA and in Canada.

22841.q: What did Triceratops have behind its head?
22841.e: Behind its head it had a wide frill made of bone. It protected the neck.
22841.m: Triceratops had a large neck frill.

22842.q: In which period of Earth's history did Triceratops live?
22842.e: Triceratops lived about 68 to 66 million years ago, at the very end of the Cretaceous.

22843.q: What does the name Triceratops mean?
22843.e: The name comes from Greek: “tri” means three, “keras” means horn and “ops” means face.

22844.q: Which large dinosaur lived at the same time as Triceratops?
22844.e: Triceratops and Tyrannosaurus rex lived at the same time. Bite marks from a T. rex have even been found on Triceratops bones.
22844.m: Triceratops and T. rex lived at the same time.

22845.q: What did the front of the mouth of Triceratops look like?
22845.e: At the front it had a pointed, hard beak like a parrot. It used it to bite off plants.
22845.m: Triceratops had a beak like a parrot.

22846.q: What did Triceratops probably need its horns for?
22846.e: It could use its horns to defend itself against attackers. Triceratops probably also fought each other with them.
22846.m: Triceratops defended itself with its horns.

22847.q: Roughly how long was a large Triceratops?
22847.e: A large Triceratops was about 8 to 9 metres long. That is almost as long as a bus.
22847.m: A Triceratops was about 8 metres long.

22848.e: A Triceratops weighed several tonnes. A car weighs only about one to two tonnes.
22848.m: A Triceratops was much heavier than a car.

22849.q: On which continent was the first Brachiosaurus found?
22849.e: The first skeleton was dug up in 1900 in the US state of Colorado.
22849.m: The first Brachiosaurus was found in North America.

22850.q: Which legs were longer on Brachiosaurus?
22850.e: Its front legs were longer than its back legs. That is why its back was higher at the front than at the back.

22851.q: What does the name Brachiosaurus mean?
22851.e: “Brachion” means arm and “sauros” means lizard. The name suits its long front legs.

22852.q: Which animal living today does Brachiosaurus remind us of with its tall neck?
22852.e: Like a giraffe, Brachiosaurus held its neck up high. That way it ate leaves high up.
22852.m: Brachiosaurus reminds us of a giraffe.

22853.q: Roughly how long was a Brachiosaurus?
22853.e: A Brachiosaurus was about 20 to 25 metres long. That is as long as two buses one behind the other.
22853.m: A Brachiosaurus was more than 20 metres long.

22854.q: How high could Brachiosaurus reach with its head?
22854.e: With its head raised it was about 9 to 13 metres tall. That is taller than a three-storey house.
22854.m: Brachiosaurus was taller than a house.

22855.e: Brachiosaurus lived in the Jurassic, about 150 million years ago.

22856.q: In which city is there a huge skeleton that was long thought to be a Brachiosaurus?
22856.e: One of the tallest dinosaur skeletons stands in the Museum of Natural History in Berlin. Today this species is called Giraffatitan.
22856.m: There is a huge long-necked dinosaur skeleton in Berlin.

a: About as big as a turkey
About as big as an elephant
About as big as a house
About as big as a mouse
22857.e: Velociraptor was only about 2 metres long, and much of that was tail. It was about as big as a turkey.
22857.m: Velociraptor was about as big as a turkey.

a: No, it ran on the ground
22858.e: Its arms were too short for proper wings. It was a fast runner on the ground.

22859.e: Velociraptor was a predator. It hunted smaller animals and ate meat.

22860.q: What did Velociraptor have on each foot?
22860.e: On its second toe it had a large, curved claw. It looked like a sickle.
22860.m: Velociraptor had a large sickle-shaped claw.

22862.q: What does the name Velociraptor mean?
22862.e: “Velox” means swift and “raptor” means robber. It was a quick hunter.

22863.q: On how many legs did Velociraptor run?
22863.e: Velociraptor ran on its two back legs. It did not need its arms for running.

22864.q: With which dinosaur was a Velociraptor found fossilised in the middle of a fight?
22864.e: A famous fossil shows a Velociraptor and a Protoceratops fighting each other. Both were buried together.
22864.m: A Velociraptor was fossilised fighting a Protoceratops.

22865.q: What was especially long on Diplodocus?
22865.e: Diplodocus had a long neck and an even longer tail.
22865.m: Diplodocus had a long neck and tail.

22866.q: Roughly how long was a Diplodocus?
22866.e: A Diplodocus grew to about 25 metres long. That is longer than two buses.
22866.m: A Diplodocus was about 25 metres long.

22867.q: What did the teeth of Diplodocus look like?
22867.e: Its teeth were as thin as pegs and sat at the front of its mouth. It used them to strip off leaves.

22868.q: How might Diplodocus have used its tail?
22868.e: Scientists think it could swing the thin tip of its tail like a whip.
22868.m: Diplodocus could probably swing its tail like a whip.

22869.q: What is the famous Diplodocus cast from the Natural History Museum in London called?
22869.e: The cast is called “Dippy”. It stood in the museum's entrance hall for many years.
22869.m: The Diplodocus cast from London is called Dippy.

22870.e: People used to think such big animals lived in water. Today we know that Diplodocus lived on land.

22871.q: What does the name Diplodocus mean?
22871.e: The name means “double beam”. It refers to special bones under its tail.

22872.q: How did Diplodocus carry its long tail when walking?
a: In the air above the ground
22872.e: Fossil footprints show no marks of a tail dragging. So Diplodocus held its tail in the air.
22872.m: Diplodocus carried its tail in the air.

22873.e: With its heavy body and short legs it was probably rather slow. Because of its protection, it did not need to run away.

22874.q: What was the back of Ankylosaurus covered with?
22874.e: Many hard bony plates and knobs covered its back. They protected it from bites.
22874.m: The back of Ankylosaurus was covered with bony plates.

22875.e: Ankylosaurus was a plant eater. Because it was built so low, it ate plants close to the ground.

22876.q: How was the body of Ankylosaurus built?
22876.e: Its body was wide and low to the ground. That made it hard to knock over.

a: At the end of the Cretaceous
At the time of the lake dwellers
22877.e: Ankylosaurus lived about 68 to 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous.
22877.m: Ankylosaurus lived at the end of the Cretaceous.

22878.q: On which continent did Ankylosaurus live?
22878.e: Ankylosaurus fossils have been found in western North America.

22879.q: Roughly how long was an Ankylosaurus?
22879.e: Depending on the estimate, an Ankylosaurus was about 6 to 9 metres long.
22879.m: An Ankylosaurus was about 8 metres long.

22880.q: What does the name Ankylosaurus mean?
22880.e: The name means “fused lizard”. Many of its bones were firmly joined together.

22881.q: What did Spinosaurus have on its back?
22881.e: It had a tall sail on its back. It was held up by long bony spines.
22881.m: Spinosaurus had a sail on its back.

22882.e: Spinosaurus mainly ate fish. But it probably also caught other animals.

22883.q: What did the snout of Spinosaurus look like?
22883.e: Its snout was long and narrow like a crocodile's. It was good for grabbing fish.
22883.m: Spinosaurus had a snout like a crocodile.

22884.e: Its fossils have been found in Egypt and Morocco. Both countries are in North Africa.

22885.q: According to current knowledge, which of these predatory dinosaurs was the longest?
22885.e: Depending on the estimate, Spinosaurus grew to about 13 to 16 metres long. It is thought to be one of the longest predatory dinosaurs.
22885.m: Spinosaurus was one of the longest predatory dinosaurs.

22886.q: Where did Spinosaurus often spend its time?
22886.e: Spinosaurus lived by large rivers. It could probably swim well too.
22886.m: Spinosaurus spent a lot of time in water.

22887.q: What happened to the first Spinosaurus bones in a museum in Munich?
a: They were destroyed in the war
22887.e: The first bones were destroyed in 1944 during the Second World War in a bombing raid. Luckily, there were drawings of them.
22887.m: The first Spinosaurus bones were destroyed in the war.

22888.q: What does the name Spinosaurus mean?
